hit.profile_notes:
According to United States - Illinois Investment Policy Board - Prohibited Investment List; Danske Bank, is removed from the Illinois Prohibited Investment List. The company was previously included in the list, deemed prohibited from investment.

According to the Financial Supervisory Authority of Norway; January 22, 2025: On January 15, 2025: the Norwegian Financial Supervisory Authority has imposed a fine against Danske Bank A/S worth NOK 50,000,000 for market manipulation in connection with the issuance of a government bond in February 2023. The Financial Supervisory Authority of Norway believes that the bank allegedly drove up the swap rate, which impacted the bond’s price and yield, and that the trades were carried out based on a deliberate strategy and in a situation where the bank profited from a high effective yield.

Аccording to the French Judicial Public Interest Agreements List; September 18, 2024: On September 18, 2024, the Paris court confirmed the judicial public interest agreement between the Paris Prosecutor's Office and Danske Bank A/S signed on August 27, 2024. A judicial investigation was opened on April 09, 2015 into organized laundering of tax fraud and concealment of organized fraud committed since January 01, 2008. It revealed that the bank's Estonian branch transferred the proceeds of tax fraud committed by an executive of a French company. Danske Bank A/S agreed to pay EUR 6,328,799 to settle the charges. 

According to storage.courtlistener.com: On January 05, 2023, Danske Bank A/S was sentenced to three years of probation for conspiracy to commit bank fraud.

According to the United States Attorney - Southern District of New York and United States Department of Justice; December 13, 2022: On December 13, 2022, Danske Bank A/S pleaded guilty to conspiring to commit bank fraud and agreed to forfeit USD 2,000,000,000 to resolve the United States investigation into Danske Bank’s fraud on U.S. banks. According to court documents, Danske Bank defrauded U.S. banks regarding Danske Bank Estonia’s customers and anti-money laundering controls to facilitate access to the U.S. financial system for Danske Bank Estonia’s high-risk customers, who resided outside of Estonia – including in Russia. The Justice Department will credit nearly USD 850,000,000 in payments that Danske Bank makes to resolve related parallel investigations by other domestic and foreign authorities. Additionally, the SEC announced a separate settlement with Danske Bank. Under the terms of that resolution, Danske Bank agreed to pay approximately USD 413,000,000, which includes a civil monetary penalty of USD 178,600,000, as well as disgorgement that will be credited to any such payments made to the Danish authorities or the department in connection with Danske Bank’s guilty plea.

According to the United States Securities and Exchange Commission; December 13, 2022: On December 13, 2022, the Securities and Exchange Commission announced fraud charges against Danske Bank for misleading investors about its anti-money laundering (AML) compliance program in its Estonian branch and failing to disclose the risks posed by the program’s significant deficiencies. Danske Bank agreed to pay USD 413,000,000 to settle the SEC’s charges.  The Securities and Exchange Commission entered a final judgment permanently enjoining Danske Bank from future violations and ordered Danske Bank to pay USD 178,600,000 in disgorgement, USD 55,800,000 in prejudgment interest, and USD 178,600,000 in a civil penalty.  According to the SEC’s complaint, when Danske Bank acquired its Estonian branch in 2007, it knew or should have known that a substantial portion of the branch’s customers were engaging in transactions that had a high risk of involving money laundering; that its internal risk management procedures were inadequate to prevent such activity; and that its AML and Know-Your-Customer procedures were not being followed and did not comply with applicable laws and rules. The SEC alleges that, from 2009 to 2016, these high-risk customers, none of whom were residents of Estonia, utilized Danske Bank’s services to transact billions of dollars in suspicious transactions through the U.S. and other countries, generating as much as 99 percent of the Estonian branch’s profits. The complaint further alleges that, although Danske Bank knew of these high-risk transactions, it made materially misleading statements and omissions in its publicly available reports stating that it complied with its AML obligations and that it had effectively managed its AML risks.

According to the Central Bank of Ireland; September 15, 2022: On September 13, 2022, the Central Bank of Ireland (the Central Bank) reprimanded and fined Danske Bank A/S, trading in Ireland as Danske Bank, EUR 1,820,000 pursuant to its Administrative Sanctions Procedure for three breaches of the Criminal Justice (Money Laundering & Terrorist Financing) Act 2010, as amended (the CJA). The three CJA breaches stem from the failure by Danske Bank A/S (Danske) to ensure that its automated transaction monitoring system monitored the transactions of certain categories of customers of its Irish branch, for a period of almost nine years, between 2010 and 2019. The root cause of this failure was historic data filters that were applied within Danske’s automated transaction monitoring system, first implemented in 2005 and rolled out to the Irish branch in 2006. Danske failed to consider the appropriateness of these historic data filters within the system or make any adjustments to the system to take account of the specific requirements of the CJA when it came into force in Ireland in 2010. This led to the erroneous exclusion of certain categories of customers from transaction monitoring, including some customers rated by Danske as high and medium risk, which caused the three breaches of the CJA in this case. The Central Bank has determined the appropriate fine to be EUR 2,600,000, which has been reduced by 30% to EUR 1,820,000 in accordance with the early settlement discount scheme provided for in the Central Bank’s Administrative Sanctions Procedure (ASP). 

According to bnn-news.com; December 16, 2020: As of December 2020, Danske Bank A/S is under investigation by US Department of the Treasury, Federal Bureau of Investigations and the US Attorney’s Office in New York over suspicions of money laundering and fraud. Danske Bank A/S has previously reported being under investigation by USA authorities for its suspicious flow of money through their branches in Baltic States.

According to the United States - CBOE Futures Exchange - CFE; January 16, 2020: On January 16, 2020, Danske Bank A/S has been ordered to pay USD 30,000 in penalty for violation of CFE rules. From in or about November 2018 to in or about January 2019, including on six trade dates, Danske submitted simultaneous buy and sell orders in the same VX futures contract expiration at the identical price for the same account. Danske submitted the matching orders in order to rebalance different sub-strategies in the account.

According to challenges.fr and danskebank.com; February 07, 2019: On February 07, 2019, Danske Bank A/S was placed under investigation in Paris, France in connection with an investigation into organized laundering of tax evasion proceeds. Reportedly, between 2007 and 2014, Danske Bank A/S might have assisted in multiple transactions consisting in investing, concealing, or converting the direct or indirect proceeds of the offenses for non-resident customers of Danske Bank’s branch in Estonia. The investigation covers transactions amounting to EUR 21,600,000. Danske Bank A/S was placed under investigation for the first time on October 11, 2017, then the bank was assigned "an assisted witness" status on January 25, 2018. 

According to irishexaminer.com; December 04, 2018: On December 2018, Danske Bank was required by the Danish Financial Supervisory Authority to add the sum of EUR 1,300,000,000 to its capital requirement so as to be prepared to alleviate the consequences of the money laundering scandal.

According to thelocal.dk; November 28, 2018: In November, 2018 Danske Bank was charged with violating money-laundering laws between February, 2007 and January, 2016. The Copenhagen international financial crimes unit SØIK reported that the investigation begun in August offered the ground for the charges.

According to reuters.com; October 04, 2018: Published on that date, Danske Bank A/S is under criminal investigation by United States authorities over a USD 230,000,000,000 money laundering scandal at its Estonian branch. The internal report of the bank said that misconduct stretching from 2007 to 2015 at the Estonian branch payments totaling USD 230,000,000,000, many of which it described as suspicious. Denmark’s Estonian branch were held by entities or individuals in Russia, which is the subject of U.S. sanctions.

According to atimes.com; September 24, 2018: In September 2018, the law firm that conducted an investigation for Danske Bank estimated that the amount of suspicious transactions at the Estonian branch of the company was EUR 200,000,000,000. The money transited through the Estonian subsidiary of Danske Bank between 2007 and 2015.

According to rte.ie; September 21, 2018: As of September 2018, Danske Bank A/S is under investigation by Britain's National Crime Agency. The agency investigates the involvement of the United Kingdom concerning the connection of money laundering at Danske Bank.

According to the yle.fi; August 06, 2018: In the ongoing investigation of Danske Bank a new leak revealed that the sum subjected to money laundering is estimated to be around EUR 7,000,000,000. It is also reported that the money laundered through the Estonian branch of Danske Bank came from Russia, Moldova and Azerbaijan. Danske Bank has started a internal investigation; the results will be revealed in September, 2018.

According to the European Securities and Markets Authority; July 23, 2018: On July 23, 2018, Danske Bank A/S was fined EUR 495,000 by the European Securities and Markets Authority for negligently breaching the Credit Rating Agencies Regulation. Danske Bank A/S issued credit ratings between June, 2011 and August, 2016 without the authorization of the European Securities and Markets Authority. 

According to dr.dk, nyheder.tv2.dk and defensenews.com; July 03, 2018: In July, 2018, in the ongoing money laundering investigation of the Estonian branch of Danske Bank, a new leak revealed the amount of DKK 25,000,000,000 in addition to the previously discovered DKK 28,000,000,000, thus, creating a total amount of DKK 53,000,000. The new amount subjected to money laundering was revealed through 20 accounts which appear in bank statements received from 20 companies that had accounts in the Estonian branch, during different periods between 2007 and 2015. The suspicious amounts were channeled to Danske Bank Estonia from Moldova, Russia and Azerbaijan and into Europe. The Danish investigators are also examining the end-uses of the money laundered for the shipment of military materials through North Korea and Iran from December, 2009.

According to the United States -Colorado Public Employees' Retirement Association: June 16, 2023: On April 04, 2018, Danske Bank A/S was removed from the restricted (i.e. scrutinized) Israel companies list published by the Colorado Public Employees' Retirement Association. On September 22, 2017, Danske Bank A/S is placed on the restricted companies list published by the Colorado Public Employees' Retirement Association.

According to the United States-Illinois State Board of Investment; January 16, 2018: On June 30, 2017, Danske Bank is included in the prohibited list, deemed prohibited from investment for having ties with entities that boycott Israel. 

According to the United States-Illinois Investment Policy Board - Prohibited Investment List; Danske Bank is added to the Illinois Prohibited Investment List, deemed prohibited from investment.

According to danskebank.dk; December 21, 2017: On December 21, 2017, Danske Bank has agreed to pay the fine of DKK 12,500,000 for violating the anti-money laundering legislation. 

According to anklagemyndigheden.dk; December 21, 2017: On December 21, 2017, Danske Bank was fined DKK 12,500,000 for violating the Money Laundering Act by the State Prosecutor for Serious Economic and International Crime. The fine came as a result of a 2016 inspection conducted by the Financial Supervisory Authority of Denmark, which showed that Danske Bank has violated the Money Laundering Act. The bank failed to follow the rules in regard to supervising transactions to and from banks which provide services on Danske Bank's behalf.      

According to euobserver.com; October 13, 2017: The Tribunal de Grande Instance de Paris stated that EUR 15,000,000 of money from organized fraud and tax evasion in Russia were moved through Danske Bank Estonian Branch into France and other EU jurisdictions from 2008 to 2011 via multiple transactions in an organized manner.

According to news.err.ee; September 05, 2017: Between 2012 and 2014, Danske Bank permitted the Azerbaijani regime to send approximately USD 2,900,000,000 of bribe money through accounts in the bank’s Estonian branch to at least two European politicians, a journalist writing regime-friendly articles, companies selling luxury goods, and other influential individuals around the world, overriding money laundering regulations.

According to reuters.com; March 21, 2017: On March 20, 2017, Danske Bank A/S has agreed to cooperate in the investigation conducted by the authorities in Moldova and Latvia. Danske Bank is suspected of money laundering operations handled through their international branches. Between 2011 and 2014, over DKK 7,000,000,000 was transferred to accounts of Danske Bank A/S and another bank. Most of the transactions were made by Danske Bank's Estonian branch.

According to United States Colorado Attorney General and the Department of Law, United States New York State Attorney General, United States Idaho Attorney General, United States Minnesota Attorney General, United States Iowa Attorney General, United States Pennsylvania Attorney General, United States Nevada Attorney General,  United States Virginia Attorney General, United States Hawaii Attorney General, United States Maine Attorney General; United States Wisconsin Department of Justice - Office of the Attorney General and United States Massachusetts Attorney General; July, 2021: On July 08, 2021, Resolution of the State’s lawsuit filed against the Sackler family and the company they controlled, Purdue Pharma, manufacturer of the blockbuster opioid drug Oxycontin and a major contributor to the deadly opioid crisis across America. The resolution of lawsuit against Purdue and the Sacklers, will make public tens of millions of documents related to Purdue’s role in the deadly opioid crisis. According to United States Attorney - District of Vermont, United States - Department of Health & Human Services, United States - Department of Justice and United States Attorney - District of New Jersey; November 24, 2020: On November 24, 2020, Opioid company Purdue Pharma LP, pleaded guilty in federal court to conspiracies to defraud the United States and to violate the Anti-Kickback Statute. Purdue pleaded guilty to an Information charging it with three felony offenses, one count of dual-object conspiracy to defraud the United States and to violate the Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, and two counts of conspiracy to violate the Federal Anti-Kickback Statute.

From May 2007 to March 2017, Purdue conspired to defraud the United States by impeding the lawful function of the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA). The misleading information comprised prescription data that included prescriptions written by doctors that Purdue had good reason to believe were engaged in diversion. The conspiracy also involved aiding and abetting violations of the Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act by facilitating the dispensing of its opioid products, including OxyContin, without a legitimate medical purpose, and thus without lawful prescriptions. Purdue also admitted it conspired to violate the Anti-Kickback Statute, between June 2009 to March 2017, by making payments to two doctors through Purdue’s physician speaker program to induce those doctors to write more prescriptions for Purdue’s opioid products.

According to United States - Maryland Attorney General, United States - Department of Justice, United States - Department of Health & Human Services, United States Attorney - District of New Jersey, United States Attorney - District of Vermont, United States Attorney - District of Maine and United States Attorney - Eastern District of Texas; October 21, 2020: On October 21, 2020 Purdue Pharma LP,  pleaded guilty to conspiracy to defraud the United States and to violate the Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, and two counts of conspiracy to violate the Federal Anti-Kickback Statute. Purdue has also agreed to a civil settlement in the amount of USD 2,800,000,000 to resolve its civil liability under the False Claims Act. Between June 2009 and March 2017, Purdue made payments to two doctors through Purdue’s doctor speaker program to induce those doctors to write more prescriptions of Purdue’s opioid products.  Similarly, from approximately April 2016 through December 2016, Purdue made payments to Practice Fusion Inc., an electronic health records company, in exchange for referring, recommending, and arranging for the ordering of Purdue’s extended-release opioid products – OxyContin, Butrans, and Hysingla.

According to United States - California Attorney General; October 03, 2019: On October 03, 2019, an amended complaint lawsuit against filed against Purdue Pharma, adding eight additional members of the Sackler family. In the lawsuit, it is alleged that Purdue misleadingly introduced OxyContin into the market as a safe and effective treatment for chronic, non-cancer pain. As early as February 1997, Purdue and certain of the Sackler defendants knew that oxycodone-containing drugs like OxyContin were among the most abused opioids in the United States. Yet, between 1996 and 2002, Purdue more than doubled its sales force, and sales rose from approximately USD 48,000,000 to nearly USD 2,000,000,000 in 2002. These sales were made by representatives falsely promoting OxyContin as a drug that was neither addictive nor subject to withdrawal symptoms, while minimizing its potential for abuse and addiction. By March 2000, Purdue was aware of specific reports made to the company about the abuse and diversion of OxyContin occurring in communities across the United States. In fact, in 2007, Purdue and a number of its executives pleaded guilty to felony misbranding of OxyContin, admitting that they illegally promoted OxyContin. Purdue agreed to pay over USD 600,000,000 in criminal and civil penalties, fines, and forfeitures.

Despite this, Purdue continued its deceptive marketing and promoting of OxyContin. Their revenues amounted to USD 3,000,000,000 in 2010, and as much as USD 1,800,000,000 as recently as 2017. The lawsuit further alleges that as part of its aggressive deceptive marketing campaign, Purdue distributed literature and other materials that misrepresented the safety of its opioid products to healthcare professionals and patients in California and elsewhere. Purdue sales representatives further pushed physicians to prescribe opioids to “trusted” patients, and implied that healthcare professionals could screen out potential addicts through urine tests and patient contracts. In addition to the amended complaint, Attorney General also joined a coalition of 23 attorneys general and formally opposed Purdue Pharma’s request to make USD 38,000,000 in bonus, incentive, and other payments to employees.

According to United States - Rhode Island Attorney General, United States - Virginia Attorney General and United States - Pennsylvania Attorney General; September 11, 2019: On September 11, 2019, The State of Rhode Island, by and through its Attorney General, brings this action pursuant to his statutory and common law authority to redress Richard S. Sacker's, Jonathan D. Sackler's, Mortimer D.A. Sackler's, Kathe A. Sackler's, Ilene Sackler Lefcourt's, David A. Sackler's, and Beverly Sackler's (together, the Sacklers) campaign to unlawfully promote and distribute opioids in Rhode Island through their control and use of Purdue Pharma, L.P.'s, Purdue Pharma Inc.'s, the Purdue Frederick Company ( together, Purdue), and the fraudulent transfer of funds generated from such sales to the Sacklers and Prescription opioid are dangerous drugs that have harmed the public health, safety and welfare affecting every community in our State causing the epidemic of opioid addiction and death.

Rhode Island government committed to continuing to aggressively pursue our claims against Purdue Pharma and the Sacklers. On September 11, 2019, filed a complaint against additional members of the Sackler family for the role that they played in the distribution of these highly addictive opioids in Rhode Island.

According to United States - Rhode Island Attorney General; August 16, 2019: Published on that date, The Lawsuit filed against Purdue Pharma L.P for pharma trafficking. The lawsuit alleges that defendant opioid manufacturers and distributors knowingly misrepresented the risk posed by prescription opioids in order expand their use and drive-up profits. It is also alleged that, in particular, opioid distributors disregarded obligations to identify suspicious orders and customers, allowing for and failing to stop the diversion of opioids within and to Rhode Island.

According to United States - Arizona Attorney General; July 31, 2019: On July 31, 2019, Lawsuit filed against Purdue Pharma LP and others for engaging in deceptive and misleading marketing to push opioids in violation of a 2007 judgment obtained by the Arizona Attorney General’s Office for violating the state’s Consumer Fraud Act.

The defendants allegedly disregarded the judgment and continued to disseminate false, misleading, or unbalanced information through Purdue’s sales representatives, advertising materials, and websites. The State also alleges that they violated the judgment by improperly marketing prescription opioids, including OxyContin, through seemingly independent nonprofits that were paid millions of dollars by Purdue to promote prescription opioids.

According to United States - Nevada Attorney General; June 17, 2019: On June 17, 2019, lawsuit filed against Purdue Pharma LP and others for violations of the Nevada Deceptive Trade Practices Act.

The lawsuit alleges that the manufacturers, distributors, pharmacies, and individuals created an ecosystem of addiction with deadly consequences to the state and its residents for their own profit. Through a systematic marketing campaign, sham “medical” organizations, funded experts, and other shameful tactics, the defendant’s peddled false science designed to demonstrate that opioids were a safe, non-addictive treatment for pain. The defendants furthered their wrongful conduct by encouraging doctors to treat addiction with more opioids and intensify the epidemic they created. Even when opioid deaths skyrocketed, the defendants simply redesigned their marketing campaign to continue to reap profits at the expense of Nevadans. Legal causes of action include violations of Nevada’s Deceptive Trade Practices Act, False Claims Act, Racketeering Act, negligence, and public nuisance.

The Complaint lists over 40 defendants. Manufacturer defendants include Purdue Pharma LP. Manufacturer Defendants have packaged, distributed, supplied, sold, placed into the stream of commerce, labeled, described, marketed, advertised, promoted and purported to warn or purported to inform prescribers and users regarding the benefits and risks associated with the use of the prescription opioid drugs. 

According to United States - Hawaii Attorney General, United States - Maine Attorney General, United States - California Attorney General and United States - District of Columbia Attorney General; June 03, 2019: Published on that date, Purdue Pharma L.P., Purdue Pharma Inc. (Purdue), certain of its affiliates, and Dr. Richard S. Sackler was sued for unlawful practices in the marketing, sale, and distribution of opioids. The lawsuit alleges that Purdue’s illegal and misleading marketing and sales practices played a major role in contributing to the nationwide opioid crisis. It further alleges that Purdue created a public nuisance through its marketing and sale of opioids and misled healthcare professionals and patients about the addictive nature of opioids and their potential for abuse and diversion.

According to United States - Iowa Attorney General, United States - Maryland Attorney General, United States - Minnesota Attorney General, United States - Oregon Department of Justice Office of the Attorney General and United States - Kansas Attorney General; May 2019: On May 2019,  law suit filed against Purdue Pharma LP for alleging that the drug company engaged in unfair, deceptive and unlawful practices in the marketing of OxyContin, helping fuel the nation’s opioid crisis.

Iowa’s lawsuit, filed in Polk County District Court, seeks restitution and civil penalties under Iowa’s Consumer Fraud Act. It alleges that Purdue, and its related companies Purdue Frederick Co., Purdue Pharmaceuticals and P.F. Laboratories, repeatedly made false and deceptive claims that OxyContin was safe and suitable for a wide range of pain patients. Specifically, the lawsuit alleges that Purdue claimed that OxyContin posed a low risk of addiction; symptoms of addiction were in fact only “pseudoaddiction” indicating the need for more opioids; long-term opioid use improved patients’ quality of life and function; and that opioids were suitable for vulnerable groups, such as elderly patients and veterans. 

According to United States Pennsylvania Attorney General; May 14, 2019: On May 02, 2019, a lawsuit was filed against Purdue Pharma, the creator of prescription painkiller OxyContin, accusing the company of a multi-faceted, illegal effort to market OxyContin in Pennsylvania. Shapiro’s suit is the first to specifically detail Purdue’s barrage of sales representatives targeting Pennsylvania doctors as a key facet of their campaign to push addictive opioids on Pennsylvanians.

The lawsuit alleges that Purdue launched an illegal marketing campaign of deception targeting Pennsylvania doctors and patients to change attitudes, practices, and the culture surrounding pain management. Some of the most egregious components of the campaign include Purdue deployed their highly trained sales staff to blanket Pennsylvania, making sales calls and in-person visits to physicians, totaling more than half a million visits in Pennsylvania alone, an amount second to only California. Purdue targeted Pennsylvania doctors with suspicious prescribing activity and would invest more sales force and marketing to get those doctors to prescribe even more OxyContin – sometimes resulting in as much as a 500% increase in OxyContin prescriptions by one office alone. Purdue misinformed doctors and pharmacists about the addictive nature of OxyContin and used industry thought leaders and in-house marketing literature to dispel the facts about the drug. As the opioid epidemic grew, Purdue created “pseudo-addiction,” a Purdue-conjured disease that showed similar equities as addiction but was to be treated, according to Purdue, with additional opioids. The Office of Attorney General is demanding that the Court issue an order preventing Purdue and anyone associated with Purdue’s misconduct from continuing to engage in these same deceptive tactics. 

According to United States Illinois Attorney General; April 08, 2019: On April 08, 2019, Lawsuit filed against Purdue Pharma L.P. and Purdue Pharma Inc. over its deceptive marketing practices designed to significantly increase prescriptions issued for opioids.

According to Raoul, between 2008 and 2017, Purdue dispatched sales representatives to Illinois hundreds of thousands of times. Raoul alleged Purdue also funded third-party publications under the guise of educational materials to promote opioids and downplay their risks, using terms like “pseudo addiction.” Sales representatives informed doctors and patients that the risks could be controlled. Despite knowing that its opioid painkillers were dangerous and being misused and diverted, Purdue allegedly targeted doctors with addicted patients and whose patients were diverting drugs for unlawful use. Raoul alleged that Purdue’s tactics tripled prescriptions of its opioids in Illinois.

According to United States Oklahoma Attorney General and United States New York State Attorney General; March 28, 2019: The lawsuit filed against Purdue Pharma LP for engaging in healthcare fraud. 

Pursuant to Executive Law § 63(12), From manufacturing, distributing, selling, or marketing opioids within the State unless it complies with heightened, independently-monitored safeguards against the recurrence of its fraudulent, illegal, and/or unlawful practices, which are to be set forth in a compliance plan reviewed and approved by Plaintiff and the Court.  Pursuant to Executive Law § 63(12), Pay restitution and damages for its fraudulent and/or illegal practices that violated that statute and caused compensable injuries to Plaintiff or any other person; and Disgorge all profits it wrongfully obtained as a result of its fraudulent and/or illegal practices in violation of that statute.

According to United States Tennessee Attorney General; March 26, 2019: On March 26, 2019, The settlement reached against purdue Pharma is a favorable development. After years of denial, Purdue finally recognized its role in creating the opioid crisis.At the same time, a recent Knox County circuit court ruling against Purdue will advance the litigation against the company for violating the state’s Consumer Protection Act. 

According to United States Utah Attorney General; January 30, 2019: The Utah Attorney General’s Office filed an administrative action against Purdue Pharma L.P. and others as part of the State’s efforts to hold accountable the opioid companies and individuals that created and fueled the opioid epidemic throughout Utah.

In the filing, under Utah Code, the Division of Consumer Protection of the Department of Commerce issued an administrative action, in the form of a citation, against the defendants alleging violations of the Utah Consumer Sales Practices Act. An administrative proceeding allows the State to seek to prove its claims and obtain a judgment, injunctive relief, and civil penalties more promptly than state district court proceedings. Based on evidence that has emerged over 2018, this administrative action alleges that not only Purdue, but two of its owners also participated in Purdue’s fraudulent conduct.

According to United States Connecticut Attorney General; December 20, 2018: The lawsuit filed against Purdue Pharma L.P. and other affiliates for alleging that they designed, financed and waged a pervasive and aggressive campaign to mislead doctors and patients, claiming that prescription opioid medications manufactured and marketed by the company were safe and effective and strategically downplaying risks of addiction that they knew were inherent in their opioid products.

The state alleges that Purdue misinformed patients and doctors to get more and more people taking its premier opioid drug, OxyContin, and its two other opioid medications, Hysingla and Butrans. Purdue allegedly led patients and doctors to believe that opioids were safe to treat even minor pain, and that patients could and should take higher and more dangerous doses. The state alleges that Purdue sent sales representatives to doctors' offices, clinics, pharmacies and hospitals in Connecticut to make deceptive sales pitches about opioid drugs; rewarded high-prescribing doctors with attention, meals, gifts and money; and awarded prizes and bonuses to sales representatives who generated the most opioid prescriptions. In Connecticut, 1038 people died of accidental drug overdoses in 2017, the vast majority from opioid-related overdoses. The Connecticut Office of the Chief Medical Examiner has projected that 1030 more people will die of overdoses in 2018. From 2013 to 2016, Connecticut experienced a fourfold increase in deaths from prescription opioid overdoses, and the estimated economic cost of the opioid epidemic in Connecticut in 2016 was USD 10,270,000,000.

Allegedly, defendants deceptively, unfairly, and unconscionably sought to convince prescribers and patients that opioids are safe, rarely addictive, and necessary for treating a wide range of common ailments. Defendants spread these myths knowing that opioids create physical dependency within days or weeks; that withdrawal from prescription opioids can be agonizing; that long-term and high-dose opioid use is particularly likely to lead to addiction; and that high doses of opioids can be fatal. Defendants at all levels of the supply chain manufacturers, distributors, and chain pharmacies continued selling opioids in Florida even though they knew or should have known that the drugs were being diverted and misused for non-medical purposes. Defendants had duties to identify and stop suspicious orders and purchases, and to put in place reasonable policies to safeguard against diversion.

It states that over the last decade Purdue has engaged in a pattern of racketeering and misleading activity in Oregon.

he complaint, filed in Multnomah Circuit Court, details how Purdue’s conduct violated an agreed upon stipulated 2007 Oregon judgment resulting from an earlier investigation of its unlawful practices, as well as four distinct Oregon laws: The Unlawful Trade Practices Act, the Elderly Persons and Persons with Disabilities Abuse Prevention Act, the False Claims Act and the Oregon Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act.

Despite some progress, the institution still has deficiencies in its systems for preventing money laundering and terrorist financing. The decision made on March 31, 2023 is final.

According to the Germany Bafin Federal Financial Supervisory Authority; November 09, 2021: On October 05, 2021, the BaFin ordered N26 Bank GmbH to take measures to ensure a proper business organization and to mitigate risks to the institution's operational resilience. In accordance with section 45b (1) sentence 1 of the German Banking Act, BaFin has ordered risk mitigation measures that place limits on customer growth and on certain risk exposures. Customer acquisition is to be substantially reduced with N26 Bank GmbH only permitted to acquire a maximum of 50 000 new customers per month. In addition, the value of exposures secured by mortgages on immovable property may not exceed EUR 500 000 000. This limitation is applicable in all countries in which N26 Bank GmbH operates. A special commissioner appointed by BaFin will monitor implementation of the measures ordered. The order has been final and binding since November 06, 2021. This order should also be considered in relation to the order issued by BaFin on May 11, 2021 to rectify deficiencies related to the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing.

According to the Germany Bafin Federal Financial Supervisory Authority; September 29, 2021: On June 25, 2021, BaFin imposed a fine in the amount of EUR 4 250 000 against N26 Bank GmbH on the basis of section 56 para. 1 no. 69 of the Act on the Detection of Proceeds from Serious Crimes (Money Laundering Act). The BaFin also ordered the bank to rectify deficiencies both in IT monitoring and in customer due diligence. In order to monitor the implementation of the measures, the BaFin is appointing a special commissioner. The notice has been final and binding since May 11, 2021.

Despite this, Purdue continued its deceptive marketing and promoting of OxyContin. Their revenues amounted to USD 3,000,000,000 in 2010, and as much as USD 1,800,000,000 as recently as 2017. hit.profile_notes:
According to U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission; December 21, 2021: The Securities and Exchange Commission announced that Nikola Corporation has agreed to pay USD 125,000,000 to settle charges that it defrauded investors by misleading them about its products, technical advancements, and commercial prospects. 

According to the SEC’s order, before Nikola had produced a single commercial product Trevor Milton, the company’s founder and former Chief Executive Officer and Executive Chairman embarked on a public relations campaign aimed at inflating and maintaining Nikola’s stock price. The order finds that Milton misled investors about Nikola’s technological advancements, in-house production capabilities, hydrogen production, truck reservations and orders, and financial outlook. The order also finds that Nikola further misled investors by misrepresenting or omitting material facts about the refueling time of its prototype vehicles, the status of its headquarters’ hydrogen station, the anticipated cost and sources of electricity for its planned hydrogen production, and the economic risks and benefits associated with its contemplated partnership with a leading auto manufacturer.

Accordingly it is hereby ordered that Nikola cease and desist from committing or causing any violations and any future violations of Section of the Exchange Act and shall pay a civil money penalty in the amount of USD 125,000,000 to the Securities and Exchange Commission.

According to cnbc.com and dailymail.co.uk; September 15, 2020: Nikola Corporation is under investigation by U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) into short seller claims that the company misled investors. details.enforcement: Conspiracy/Burglary/Stolen Property | CO-Fiscalía General de la Nación, República de Colombia | Colombia

hit.profile_notes:
According to Fiscalía General de la Nación de Colombia; March 31, 2026: Published on that date, the authorities were able to charge Duban Estiben Saldarriaga Caro, Medardo de Jesús Jaramillo Álvarez, Juan David Echeverri Giraldo, Luis Alberto David Uribe, Sebastián Giraldo Atehortua, Guillermo José García Zabaleta, Hernan Dario Zapata López, Yeferson Hincapié Henao, Juan Carlos Londoño González, Adrián Antonio Guisao Serna, and Juan Diego Uribe Zapata with conspiracy and aggravated theft. These individuals are alleged members of a criminal network accused of stealing components from communications antenna base stations in the municipalities of the Aburrá Valley. According to the information, these individuals allegedly used tools such as grinders, shears, sledgehammers, hammers, and crowbars to illegally enter the sites and steal lithium and lead-acid batteries, copper cables, and generators. They also allegedly transported the stolen items in vehicles and later sold the batteries and generators at low prices. The defendants did not accept the chartes. Six of the defendants were placed under pre-trial detention in prison and four under house arrest. 


De acuerdo con Fiscalía General de la Nación de Colombia; Marzo 31, 2026: Publicado en dicha fecha, las autoridades lograron imputar por los delitos de concierto para delinquir y hurto calificado y agravado a Duban Estiben Saldarriaga Caro, Medardo de Jesús Jaramillo Álvarez, Juan David Echeverri Giraldo, Luis Alberto David Uribe, Sebastián Giraldo Atehortua, Guillermo José García Zabaleta, Hernan Dario Zapata López, Yeferson Hincapié Henao, Juan Calos Londoño González, Adrián Antonio Guisao Serna y Juan Diego Uribe Zapata, presuntos integrantes de una red delincuencial señalada de hurtar elementos de las estaciones base de antenas de comunicaciones en los municipios del Valle de Aburrá. De acuerdo con la información, estas personas mediante el uso de herramientas como pulidoras, cizallas, mazos, almádanas, barras, entre otros elementos, al parecer, ingresaban de manera irregular a los lugares para hurtar baterías de litio y plomo, cables de cobre y plantas eléctricas. Asimismo, presuntamente movilizaban los elementos hurtados en vehículos y posteriormente vendías las baterías y plantas a bajo costo. Los procesados no aceptaron cargos. Seis de los acusados fueron cobijados con medida de aseguramiento en establecimiento carcelario y cuatro en lugar de domicilio.

hit.profile_notes:
According to the Germany Bafin Federal Financial Supervisory Authority; December 15, 2025: N26 Bank SE must take appropriate and effective measures to establish a proper business organization. This was ordered by the financial regulator BaFin. BaFin has also appointed a special representative who will monitor compliance with the measures and report to BaFin on the progress of implementation. In addition, BaFin has set additional capital requirements and business restrictions for the institution. The bank is no longer allowed to conduct new business with mortgage loans in the Netherlands. The institute is also prohibited from securitizing claims from this transaction.

According to the Germany Bafin Federal Financial Supervisory Authority; May 21, 2024: The Federal Financial Supervisory Authority BaFin has imposed a fine of EUR 9 200 000 on N26 Bank AG for systematically late submission of suspicious transaction report in 2022. The fine notice is legally binding.

According to the Germany Bafin Federal Financial Supervisory Authority; July 17, 2023: On March 31, 2023, the Financial Supervisory Authority (BaFin) extended anti-money laundering measures against N26 Bank AG in addition to its order made on May 11, 2021, and specified them. The growth restrictions for new customers and the mandate of the special representative remain in place. Despite some progress, the institution still has deficiencies in its systems for preventing money laundering and terrorist financing. The decision made on March 31, 2023 is final.

According to the Germany Bafin Federal Financial Supervisory Authority; November 09, 2021: On October 05, 2021, the BaFin ordered N26 Bank GmbH to take measures to ensure a proper business organization and to mitigate risks to the institution's operational resilience. In accordance with section 45b (1) sentence 1 of the German Banking Act, BaFin has ordered risk mitigation measures that place limits on customer growth and on certain risk exposures. Customer acquisition is to be substantially reduced with N26 Bank GmbH only permitted to acquire a maximum of 50 000 new customers per month. In addition, the value of exposures secured by mortgages on immovable property may not exceed EUR 500 000 000. This limitation is applicable in all countries in which N26 Bank GmbH operates. A special commissioner appointed by BaFin will monitor implementation of the measures ordered. The order has been final and binding since November 06, 2021. This order should also be considered in relation to the order issued by BaFin on May 11, 2021 to rectify deficiencies related to the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing.

According to the Germany Bafin Federal Financial Supervisory Authority; September 29, 2021: On June 25, 2021, BaFin imposed a fine in the amount of EUR 4 250 000 against N26 Bank GmbH on the basis of section 56 para. 1 no. 69 of the Act on the Detection of Proceeds from Serious Crimes (Money Laundering Act). The decision came into force on July 15, 2021.

According to the Germany Bafin Federal Financial Supervisory Authority; May 12, 2021: On May 11, 2021, the German Federal Financial Supervisory Authority (BaFin) ordered N26 Bank GmbH to implement appropriate internal controls and safeguards and comply with general due diligence requirements, in order to prevent money laundering and terrorist financing. The BaFin also ordered the bank to rectify deficiencies both in IT monitoring and in customer due diligence. In order to monitor the implementation of the measures, the BaFin is appointing a special commissioner. The notice has been final and binding since May 11, 2021.

According to the Germany Bafin Federal Financial Supervisory Authority; May 22, 2019: On May 20, 2019, the German Federal Financial Supervisory Authority (BaFin) issued an order against N26 Bank GmbH to take appropriate internal safety measures and to comply with general Customer Due Diligence obligations. Moreover, N26 Bank GmbH has to ensure the existence of an adequate personnel and technical-organisational equipment in order to comply with its obligations under money laundering law. The decision became legal on May 20, 2019.

hit.name: Francisco Corrêa de Lima
hit.position_or_allegation: Fined for fraud and embezzlement - June 08, 2021.

details.enforcement: Embezzlement | BR - Ministério Público do Estado do Amazonas | Brazil

hit.profile_notes:
According to tjam.jus.br; June 08, 2021: Francisco Corrêa de Lima was sentenced for fraud and embezzlement. According to investigations, in November, 2007, Corrêa de Lima was involved in fraud committed in an agreement intended for the execution of works to improve and expand the road system in five cities in the interior of Amazonas State. Through an inspection it was found that the works requested were not executed as reported, even when the state transferred BRL 17,246,010.10 out of the BRL 34,943,716.30 stated in the contract. Corrêa de Lima had his political rights suspended for five years, public function suspended, and was fined 10 times the amount received as profit at the time the facts took place.

According to BR - Ministério Público do Estado do Amazonas: September 03, 2019: On August 27, 2019, the Public Ministry of Amazonas accused Seinfra supervisor Francisco Corrêa de Lima and other individuals of administrative misconduct in the construction of a bridge in the Philadelphia Community, in the rural area of Santo Antônio do Iça. According to the complaint, the construction of the bridge began between June and August 2006 reaching BRL 1,600,000,000.00, however, on June 21, 2010, the State Court of Audits found that the bridge had collapsed.

According to consultasaj.tjam.jus.br; April 29, 2009: The Court of Justice received the complaint filed by the Public Ministry of Amazonas against Francisco Corrêa de Lima and others for fraud and embezzlement. According to the complaint, the group was involved in fraud committed in a contract valued at BRL 34,943,716.30.


De acordo com tjam.jus.br; Junho 08, 2021: Francisco Corrêa de Lima foi condenado por fraude e peculato. Segundo investigações, em Novembro de 2007, Corrêa de Lima esteve envolvido em fraude cometida em convênio destinado à execução de obras de melhoria e ampliação do sistema viário em cinco municípios do interior do Estado do Amazonas. Por meio de fiscalização, constatou-se que as obras solicitadas não foram executadas conforme informado, mesmo quando o estado repassou BRL 17.246.010,10 dos BRL 34.943.716,30 previstos em contrato. Corrêa de Lima teve seus direitos políticos suspensos por cinco anos, função pública suspensa e foi multado em 10 vezes o valor recebido a título de lucro na época dos fatos.

De acordo com BR - Ministério Público do Estado do Amazonas: Setembro 03, 2019: Em Agosto 27, 2019, o Ministério Público do Amazonas acusou o fiscal da Seinfra, Francisco Corrêa de Lima, e outros indivíduos de improbidade administrativa na construção da Ponte na Comunidade Filadélfia, na zona rural do Município. Segundo a denúncia, a construção da ponte começou entre junho e agosto de 2006 atingindo o valor de BRL 1.600.000.000,00, no entanto, no dia 21 de junho de 2010, o Tribunal de Contas do Estado verificou que a ponte entrou em colapso e desabou.

De acordo com consultasaj.tjam.jus.br; Abril 29, 2009: O Tribunal de Justiça recebeu denúncia do Ministério Público do Amazonas contra Francisco Corrêa de Lima e outros por fraude e peculato. De acordo com a denúncia, o grupo estava envolvido em fraude cometida em contrato no valor de BRL 34.943.716,30.

Abdul Rahman Yasin was born on 10 April 1960.

On December 31, 2020, the United Kingdom under the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office added ABDUL RAHMAN YASIN under its sanctions list. 

On November 24, 2016, the Trinidad and Tobago Financial Intelligence Unit listed ABDUL RAHMAN on its Targeted Financial Sanctions List.

On March 17, 2016, ABDUL RAHMAN YASIN was added to the Indonesian Financial Transaction Reports and Analysis Center Suspected Terrorists and Terrorist Organizations list.

On October 17, 2001, the United Nations Security Council imposed sanctions on ABDUL RAHMAN YASIN for being associated with Al-Qaida. Yasin directly assisted terrorist mastermind Ramzi Ahmed Yousef in carrying out the February 26, 1993, World Trade Center bombing in New York City. Yasin fled the United States immediately after the bombing to avoid arrest. He was indicted in the United States for his role in the World Trade Center bombing. He is wanted for his alleged participation in the terrorist bombing of the World Trade Center, New York City, on February 26, 1993, which resulted in six deaths, the wounding of numerous individuals, and the significant destruction of property and commerce.

On October 17, 2001, ABDUL RAHMAN YASIN was added to Argentina Registro Público de Personas y Entidades Vinculadas a Actos de Terrorismo y su Financiamiento-Sanctions List.

Abdul Rahman Yasin has been added to the sanctions Switzerland's State Secretariat for Economic Affairs under the ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaeda regime.

Abdul Rahman Yasin has been added to the European Union Council Implementing Regulation (EU) 866/2003 imposing specific restrictive measures against persons and entities associated with Usama bin Laden, the Al-Qaida network and the Taliban.

Abdul Rahman YASIN has been added to the New Zealand Police List - Designated terrorist entity pursuant to UNSC 1267/1989/2253.

The Rewards For Justice Program, United States Department of State, is offering a reward of up to USD 25,000,000 for information leading directly to the apprehension or conviction of Abdul Rahman Yasin.

Abdul Yasin was born in 1960 in Bloomington, Ind., where his Iraqi father was a graduate student, and grew up in Baghdad. He returned to the United States in the early 1990's, to live with his mother and a brother who were living in Jersey City. It was then that he met Ramzi Yousef. Yousef recruited Yasin for the plot to blow up the World Trade Center. Mr. Yasin helped mix the chemicals used in the blast, at one point severely burning his leg. 

Abdul Yasin lived with several of the WTC conspirators at 34 Kensington Ave in Jersey City. The FBI initially detained Mr. Yasin after the attack and then released him. After it realized its error, the FBI placed Abdul Yasin on the list of "Most Wanted" terrorists, but it was too late. On the evening of March 5th, Yasin departed the United States on a Royal Jordanian Airlines flight. The FBI believes that Yasin flew to Jordan and then drove twelve hours to Baghdad, where he has relatives. 

A reporter for ABC News spotted Yasin in Baghdad in 1994 and reported that he was operating freely. A neighbor told the reporter that Yasin was working for the Iraqi government. Documents recovered from postwar Iraq indicate that Yasin received no only safe haven in Iraq, but also funding from the former Iraqi regime. In an interview with the CBS News program "60 Minutes" in June 2002, Mr. Yasin admitted his involvement in the World Trade Center bombing and expressed regret for what he had done. "I'm very sorry for what happened," he said. "I don't know what to do to make it up." Abdul Rahman Yasin is still at large. The United States Department of State is offering a reward of up to $5 million for information leading directly to his apprehension or conviction. 

Yasin is believed to still be in Iraq.

Yasin fled the United States immediately after the bombing to avoid arrest. After the bombing, law enforcement officials obtained evidence which led to the indictment and arrest of several suspected terrorists involved in the bombing, including Yasin. hit.name: Juan Reyes
hit.position_or_allegation: Convicted and disqualified from holding public office for embezzlement and aggravated conspiracy.

details.enforcement: Conspiracy/Disqualified/Organized Crime/Embezzlement | PE-Ministerio Público, Fiscalia de la Nación (Perú) | Peru

hit.profile_notes:
According to Ministerio Público, Fiscalía de la Nación del Perú; February 11, 2026: The Provincial Prosecutor's Office Specializing in Corruption Crimes by Officials in Lambayeque obtained an 18-year prison sentence for the former mayor of the Provincial Municipality of San Ignacio, Carlos Martínez, for the crime of embezzlement. He was also fined 620 days and disqualified from holding public office for 10 years. Along with him, other officials were also convicted of the same crime. Among them were the former manager of Territorial Planning and Urban Infrastructure, Álvaro Cabrera; the former head of Settlements, José Larraín; the former head of Logistics, Wilfredo Rivera; the former head of Treasury, Roel Aldana; and the former assistant to the Works Settlement office, William Díaz, who received sentences of up to 18 years in prison and were disqualified from holding public office. Likewise, José Larraín, Juan Reyes, and Luis Ancajima were convicted as accomplices to the crime of aggravated conspiracy, as they were members of the criminal organization "Los topos de San Ignacio". Manuel Ilatoma Gálvez was also convicted in this case, receiving a sentence of four years and 25 days in prison and a three-year disqualification from public office. José Zeña, Juan Ramos, Juan Nanfuñay, and Daniel Pisfil were also convicted. According to the report, they all embezzled PEN 762,000 in public funds by simulating contracts for alleged services involving the preparation of layout plans and topographic surveys.


De acuerdo con Ministerio Público, Fiscalía de la Nación del Perú; Febrero 11, 2026: La Fiscalía Provincial Especializada en Delitos de Corrupción de Funcionarios de Lambayeque logró una condena de 18 años de prisión para el exalcalde de la Municipalidad Provincial de San Ignacio, Carlos Martínez, por el delito de peculado doloso por apropiación. Asimismo, se le impuso una multa de 620 días multa y una inhabilitación para el ejercicio de la función pública por 10 años. Junto a él, también se obtuvo la sentencia de otros funcionarios por el mismo delito. Entre ellos el exgerente de Acondicionamiento Territorial e Infraestructura Urbana, Álvaro Cabrera; el exjefe de Liquidaciones, José Larraín; el exjefe de Logística, Wilfredo Rivera; el exjefe de Tesorería, Roel Aldana; y el exasistente de la oficina de Liquidación de Obras, William Díaz, quienes recibieron penas de hasta 18 años de prisión y fueron inhabilitados para ejercer la función pública. Asimismo, José Larraín, Juan Reyes y Luis Ancajima fueron sentenciados como cómplices del delito de asociación ilícita en su forma agravada, ya que fueron miembros de la organización criminal "Los topos de San Ignacio". Por este caso, también fue condenado Manuel Ilatoma Gálvez, quien recibió una sentencia de cuatro años y 25 días de prisión y una inhabilitación por tres años. También fueron condenados José Zeña, Juan Ramos, Juan Nanfuñay, Daniel Pisfil. De acuerdo con el informe, todos ellos se apropiaron de PEN 762 000 de fondos públicos, mediante la simulación de contratos por presuntos servicios de elaboración de planos de replanteo y levantamiento topográfico.

hit.name: Michael David Taylor
hit.position_or_allegation: Fined USD 5,000 and suspended from association with any Financial Industry Regulatory Authority member in any capacity for three months for violating the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority rule - April 08, 2016.

details.enforcement: Debarred/Disciplined | US –Financial Industry Regulatory Authority | United States

hit.profile_notes: According to United States-Financial Industry Regulatory Authority; June 2016: On April 08, 2016, Michael David Taylor was assessed a deferred fine of USD 5,000 and suspended from association with any FINRA member in any capacity for three months. Without admitting or denying the findings, Taylor consented to the sanctions and to the entry of findings that he circumvented his member firm’s annuity replacement procedures by failing to identify and submit variable annuity purchases totaling approximately USD 700,000 as annuity replacements, even though each purchase was funded by the sale of another annuity. The findings stated that Taylor concealed the replacement transactions from the firm’s supervisory review by transferring the proceeds from the replaced annuity to a firm money market account in the customer’s name. After waiting approximately 30 to 60 days, Taylor then used the funds in the money market account to purchase the new variable annuity. Taylor further concealed that the annuity purchases were replacements by providing inaccurate information on the transaction documents he submitted to the firm and the annuity companies. Taylor earned approximately USD 18,000 in additional commissions by submitting the annuity purchases as new trades rather than as annuity replacements. Taylor subsequently repaid these commissions to the firm. The suspension is in effect from April 18, 2016 to July 17, 2016.

hit.profile_notes:
According to the Federal Bureau of Prisons, information as of December 13, 2017:
Name: TIMOTHY PANGELIN VILLAGOMEZ
Register Number: 00590-005
Age: 55
Race: Asian
Sex: Male
Released On: June 23, 2017

According to the pina.com.fj; June 13, 2013: On June 12, 2013, Timothy Pangelinan Villagomez, former Lieutenant Governor of the Northern Mariana Islands, was resentenced to hundred and eight months imprisonment, or nine years, from the original eighty seven months for his role in the Rydlyme corruption scandal. After an 18-day trial almost four years ago, Villagomez was convicted of conspiracy to defraud the United States, wire fraud, theft concerning a program receiving federal funds, and bribery concerning a program receiving federal funds that involved the Commonwealth Utilities Corp.

According to the saipantribune.com; August 06, 2009: On August 05, 2009, Timothy Pangelinan Villagomez, former Lieutenant Governor, was sentenced to eighty seven months in prison and three years of supervised release for his role in the Rydlyme corruption scandal. Judge ordered Villagomez and the Santos couple to jointly pay USD 346,125 to the court for reimbursement to CUC. Judge also ordered Villagomez and the Santos couple to each pay a USD 400 court assessment fee and perform 200 hours of community service. Villagomez and the Santos couple were found guilty on April 24, 2009, of all charges relating to CUC's purchases of excessive amounts of a chemical, at a 400 percent markup, from companies owned by James and Joaquina Santos.

According to the saipantribune.com; August 12, 2008: On August 11, 2008, Former Lt. Gov. Timothy Villagomez entered a federal court in handcuffs to face an indictment on three felony counts of wire fraud, conspiracy and theft of federal funds, the culmination of an extensive five-month investigation by federal authorities. The indictment, charges Villagomez, Commerce Secretary James Santos, his wife Joaquina Santos-who is Villagomez's sister-and former Commonwealth Utilities Corp. executive director Anthony Guerrero with conspiring to bilk the CNMI government out of thousands of dollars through business deals involving needless chemical purchases for CUC. Villagomez and the Santos' pleaded not guilty to each of the charges against them.

On the evening of March 5th, Yasin departed the United States on a Royal Jordanian Airlines flight. The FBI believes that Yasin flew to Jordan and then drove twelve hours to Baghdad, where he has relatives. 

A reporter for ABC News spotted Yasin in Baghdad in 1994 and reported that he was operating freely. A neighbor told the reporter that Yasin was working for the Iraqi government. Documents recovered from postwar Iraq indicate that Yasin received no only safe haven in Iraq, but also funding from the former Iraqi regime. In an interview with the CBS News program "60 Minutes" in June 2002, Mr. Yasin admitted his involvement in the World Trade Center bombing and expressed regret for what he had done. "I'm very sorry for what happened," he said. "I don't know what to do to make it up." Abdul Rahman Yasin is still at large. According to United States Attorney - Southern District of New York and U.S. Internal Revenue Service; September 12, 2023: Karl Sebastian Greenwood was sentenced to 20 years in prison for his orchestration of the massive OneCoin fraud scheme. Greenwood was ordered to pay approximately USD 300 million in forfeiture.

According to United States Attorney - Southern District of New York and U.S. Internal Revenue Service; December 16, 2022: On December 16, 2022, Karl Sebastian Greenwood, who co-founded OneCoin, pled guilty to one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, one count of wire fraud and one count of conspiracy to commit money laundering in connection with his participation in the massive OneCoin fraud scheme.  OneCoin, which began operations in 2014 and was based in Sofia, Bulgaria, marketed and sold a fraudulent cryptocurrency by the same name through a global multi-level-marketing (MLM) network.  As a result of misrepresentations that Greenwood and others made about OneCoin, victims invested over four billion dollars worldwide in the fraudulent cryptocurrency. 

Greenwood and his co-conspirators, including fugitive Ruja Ignatova, conned unsuspecting victims out of billions of dollars, claiming that OneCoin would be the Bitcoin killer.  In fact, OneCoins were entirely worthless. OneCoin operated as a MLM network through which members received commissions for recruiting others to purchase cryptocurrency packages.  Greenwood and other OneCoin leaders also claimed that the OneCoin cryptocurrency was “mined” using mining servers maintained and operated by the company.  In fact, OneCoins were never mined using computer resources. Greenwood was arrested at his residence on the island of Koh Samui, Thailand, in July 2018, and was extradited to the United States to face fraud and money laundering charges in October 2018. Greenwood has been detained since his arrest in July 2018.

hit.profile_notes:
According to the India National Investigation Agency; July 24, 2024: On July 24, 2024, Abdul Rahman, son of Ahamed Mansoor was accused along with others of terrorism. A case registered in FIR No RC-02/2024/NIA/CHE under sections 34 and 153B of Indian Penal Code 1860 and section 13 of Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967. The Central Government has received information from Government of Tamil Nadu regarding registration of FIR No. 173/2024 dated May 21, 2024, at PS Chennai City, District CCD-I, Tamil Nadu under sections 153B & 34 of Indian Penal Code and section 13 of Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 relating to arrest of one Dr. Hameed Hussain, who is the chief coordinator of an Islamic organization, called HuT (Hizb-ut-Tahrir) and has been holding secret meetings, on its behalf, with groups of people, at MEET (Modern Essential Education Trust) Hall at Johny John Khan road, Chennai, and has been running a campaign throughout Tamil Nadu to establish Khalifah/Islamic rule in India, and is striving to divide the people by acting against the sovereignty of the country. And whereas, the Central Government is of the opinion that Scheduled Offence under National Investigation Agency Act, 2008 has been committed, and having regard to the gravity of the offence and its international and national ramifications with interstate linkages, it is required to be investigated by National Investigation Agency in accordance with the National Investigation Agency Act, 2008.

According to the indianexpress.com; August 01, 2024: On May 25, 2024, Abdul Rahman was arrested along with others under the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act after receiving information from central agencies. Hussain and his associates have been running a campaign throughout Tamil Nadu to establish Khalifah/Islamic rule in India and are striving to divide the people by acting against the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the country,” stated the FIR registered under Indian Penal Code section 153B (imputations, assertions prejudicial to national integration) and section 13 (advocating, abetting or inciting any unlawful activity) of the UAPA.

relationships: Global Asset Financial Services Group, LLC (AffiliatedCompany
hit.profile_notes:
According to U.S. Federal Trade Commission; December 11, 2019: On December 06, 2019 Omar Hussain and others were ordered to pay jointly and severally USD 8,877,564 for engaging in deceptive practice. The defendants were permanently banned from the debt collection business and from misleading consumers about debt in a settlement with the Federal Trade Commission. In addition to being banned from debt collection, debt brokering activities, and misleading consumers, the defendants also will be banned from misrepresenting to consumers whether they are attorneys.

According to U.S. Federal Trade Commission; February 08, 2019: On February 04, 2019, a federal court has temporarily halted and frozen the assets of a debt collection scheme that allegedly bilked consumers out of millions of dollars, using deceptive and threatening tactics to collect phantom debts that they did not owe. Omar Hussain and others falsely claimed to be attorneys or affiliated with attorneys to pressure consumers into making payments on debts they did not owe, and threatened to take legal action against consumers if they did not pay. The complaint charged that the Omar Hussain deceptive and unfair tactics violated the FTC Act and the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act. Hussain is or was a manager, director, president, or organizer of Trans America, Midwestern Alliance, TACS I,  TACS II , TACS III, and Cedar Rose. He is or was an authorized signatory on the bank and merchant accounts for many of the Defendants. At all times material to this complaint, acting alone or in concert with others, he has formulated, directed, controlled, had the authority to control, or participated in the acts and practices set forth in this Complaint.

hit.profile_notes:
According to U.S. Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation; May 10, 2021: The Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation announced a settlement with Umpqua Bank for engaging in unfair and deceptive practices, in violation of Section 5 of the Federal Trade Commission Act (Section 5). Umpqua Bank stipulated to the issuance of an Order to Pay Civil Money Penalty (CMP) in the amount of USD 1,800,000.

The FDIC determined that Umpqua Bank engaged in Section 5 violations related to collection practices involving commercial equipment financing through its wholly owned subsidiary, Financial Pacific Leasing, Inc.. The FDIC determined that FinPac’s collection fee practices were unfair and deceptive. Specifically, FinPac charged various undisclosed collection fees to borrowers whose accounts were past due, such as collection call and letter fees and third-party collection fees.

The FDIC also determined that certain collection practices at FinPac were unfair and deceptive. FinPac engaged in excessive and sequential collection calls to customers, even when customers requested that FinPac stop these calls. FinPac also disclosed information about the customers’ debts to third parties. Lastly, FinPac advised borrowers FinPac would report delinquencies on commercial debt to the consumer reporting agencies, when its policy and practice was not to report such delinquencies to the consumer reporting agencies. Umpqua Bank agreed to the issuance of the Order without admitting or denying these violations. In addition, the Bank voluntarily paid restitution totaling approximately USD 1,628,000 to the 16,902 customers who were charged the undisclosed collection fees.

According to U.S. Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation; May 06, 2021; Umpqua Bank ordered to pay penalty of USD 1,800,000 for engaged in violations of Section 5 of the Federal Trade Commission Act. 

According to U.S. FDIC Temporary Order to Cease and Desist and U.S. Washington State Department of Financial Institutions Securities Division; September 27, 2010: The Cease and Desist order against Sterling Savings Bank has been terminated.

According to the U.S. FDIC Order to Cease and Desist and U.S. Washington State Department of Financial Institutions Securities Division; October 9, 2009: Cease and desist order issued against Sterling Savings Bank from the following unsafe and unsound banking practices, as more fully set forth in the joint FDIC and WDFI Report of Visitation dated June 29, 2009. The FDIC and the WDFI considered the matter and determined that they had reason to believe that the Bank had engaged in unsafe or unsound banking practices and violations of law and/or regulations. Sterling Savings Bank  failed to maintain the minimum capital ratio, failed to submit an acceptable capital plan and failed to implement or adhere to a capital plan to which the Regional Director and the Director of Banks have taken no written objection.
