hit.profile_notes:
According to elpais.com; October 28, 2021: Luis Bárcenas was sentenced to two years in prison for forgery, fraud and tax evasion. The National Court issued a ruling in relation to the reform of the headquarters of the Popular Party (PP) after having considered proven that Bárcenas paid the Unifica company more than EUR 1,000,000 outside of the official billing and accounting, funds that were not declared to the Public Treasury. According to the Hearing, Bárcenas managed the cash funds that were contributed to the PP as private donations through a parallel accounting, of which the income and expenses were not recorded in the official accounting and, therefore, were not audited by the Court of Accounts. Consequently, a fine of EUR 1,200,000 was imposed on Bárcenas for having been a necessary cooperator of a crime of accounting falsification in relation to another against the Treasury for the fraud to the treasury of the Unifica Corporation Tax of 2007.

According to elconfidencial.com; February 22, 2021: The National High Court agreed to commence the repatriation of EUR 50,342,107 that different convicted persons in the Gürtel case, among whom was Luis Bárcenas, had in Switzerland. The objective was to have at the disposal of the court the amounts that had been blocked in various banks in the aforementioned country, which included Credit Suisse, Lombard Odier, LGT Bank, Banque SYZ and Mirabaud. According to the decree, around EUR 22,400,000 were in accounts owned by Bárcenas.

According to antena3.com; February 08, 2021: On February 08, 2021, Luis Bárcenas was facing trial for corruption, forgery and tax evasion. The case was related to the alleged box B of the Popular Party (PP), which is why Bárcenas was going to have to answer for the irregular payment of the reform of the headquarters of the PP on Genova street and for the purchase of shares of a half with money from box B. Likewise, Bárcenas exposed as responsible for an irregular financing institutionalized since 1982, the old leadership headed by Mariano Rajoy.

According to elmundo.es; October 14, 2020: The Supreme Court notified the sentence of the piece Epoca I of the Gürtel plot (1999 - 2005), confirming the sentences imposed by the National High Court on the main leaders of the corruption network as well as that of the Popular Party. The Chamber upheld the sentence of the leader of the plot; however, it reduced the sentences for several of those involved, among them, Luis Bárcenas, who was reduced to 29 years and one month in prison. The Supreme Court took into consideration the appeal of Bárcenas, resulting in the reduction of the sentence for money laundering, exclusion of the crime of forgery and the acquittal of the crime of procedural fraud.

According to nuevodiariodesalta.com.ar; June 02, 2018: Luis Barcenas was part of the case where the La Moraleja Company was involved in a plot of crimes of corruption and money laundering, in which Ángel Sanchis, Ángel Sanchis Herrero were the main architects after diverting EUR 3,000,000 through the company mentioned. The ruling mentions Bárcenas as a fundamental piece, who granted the aforementioned amount to Sanchis Perales as a loan on behalf of the Sinequanon Foundation, however, the funds came out of the Bárcenas account in the name of the Panamanian foundation that the latter had in the Dresdner Bank of Switzerland towards another of the HSBC in New York in charge of Brixo SA, an entity in Uruguay linked to the Sanchís family. Subsequently, part of the funds were transferred to accounts of another Sanchis company, Argentina's La Moraleja SA, through which the aforementioned individuals devised a complex scheme to reimburse the money to Bárcenas. Consequently, all those involved received their respective convictions after it was verified that these knew the illicit origin of the funds.

According to vanitatis.elconfidencial.com; May 24, 2018: Luis Bárcenas was sentenced to 33 years in prison for money laundering, tax evasion, forgery and fraud. Luis Bárcenas and other associates were involved in the Gürtel case and used Grupo Correa and Partido Popular to issue inflated invoices or invoices that did not respond to real services and were paid out of municipal public funds.

According to lainformacion.com; October 02, 2016: The trial of the case Gürtel was schedule on October 04, 2016. The defendants were 37 people including Jose Luis Barcenas Gutierrez, who were accused of fraud, corruption, financial crimes, bribery, forgery and embezzlement for committing irregular activities developed between the years 1999 and 2005. The oral hearing would take place in the headquarters in San Fernando de Henares.

According to efe.com; April 27, 2015: The Prosecutor's Office requested 5 years in prison and fined EUR 265,000 against José Luis Bárcenas Gutiérrez for the "Bárcenas case". Based on the prosecutor, during 1990 to 2009, when Bárcenas was Treasurer and Manager of Partido Popular (PP), he received cash funds by entrepreneurs who could not made donations to the party, since it was against the law.
 
According to lavozdegalicia.es; March 06, 2015: The Judge of the National Audience ordered the trial of 40 individuals for alleged involvement in a kickback scheme at the heart of Partido Popular (PP). Jose Luis Barcenas was one of the 40 individuals and master head of the case.

According to 20minutos.es; January 22, 2015: A Judge of the National Audience gave José Luis Bárcenas bail, after paying EUR 200,000. Additionally, Bárcenas must appear before the National Court every Monday, Wednesday and Friday, give his address and remain in Spain. 

According to elmundo.es; February 26, 2014: A report of the National Department of Fraud Investigation (ONIF), revealed that the Former Judge of the National Audience has rejected for the third time a request by Bárcenas Gutiérrez to be release from prison, after disclosure of  two bank accounts in the United States under his name.  Bárcenas Gutiérrez defrauded the Spanish Internal Revenue Office with a total EUR 11,5 00,000 between 2000 and 2011. 

According to lavozdegalicia.es; December 20, 2013: The National Audience confirmed the confinement of Jose Luis Bárcenas Gutiérrez, since they considered he could escape to a country that would not allowed his extradition.

According to canarias24horas.com; July 30, 2013: A Judge of the National Audience decided to foreclosure of the bank accounts in Spain and property of the former Treasurer of Partido Popular (PP), Jose Luis Bárcenas Gutiérrez, after the period of time to pay the civil bond of EUR 43,200,000 imposed by the Court expired. 

According to elpais.com; July 23, 2013: The judge in charge of the Gürtel case, Pablo Ruz, requested to the Uruguayan authorities to freeze all the bank accounts under the name of Jose Luis Bárcenas Gutiérrez or his company Tesedul, which was allegedly the front for laundering money. 

According to publico.pt; June 27, 2013: The Former Treasurer of Partido Popular (PP), José Luis Bárcenas, was arrested for flight risk. Bárcenas was accused of allegedly sending large sums of money from the political party's accounts to Switzerland and USA. He was sent to prison without bail, as there was a serious risk of flight, or possible manipulation and alteration of evidence of a false purchase and sale of works of art. Bárcenas was to testify on June 27, 2013, about the entry of EUR 500,000 on his account in the notes of EUR 500 during 2006. Bárcenas claimed the money was from sales of art works. He was being investigated for allegedly committing crimes against the government and against public finance, money laundering, attempted fraud and misrepresentation in commercial document.

According to elpais.com; June 13, 2013: According to the report of the Spanish Tax Office, José Luis Bárcenas and his wife, Rosalía Iglesias, defrauded the Spanish Internal Revenue Service with EUR 1,500,000 in 2002 and 2003. The couple also got tax returns of EUR 21,795 during those years. 

According to 20minutos.es; January 16, 2013: According to the reports that judge Pablo Ruz sent to the authorities, the former senator Jose Luis Bárcenas had EUR 22,000,000 in Swiss bank accounts, that were transferred to another account when he was charged with corruption for his involvement in the Gürtel case. 

According to rtve.es; February 09, 2009: Luis Bárcenas was provisionally indicted for corruption, bribery and tax evasion within Operation Gürtel. The Gürtel case investigated a presumed plot of corruption and influence peddling led by the businessman Francisco Correa, who drew funds from public entities in the autonomous communities of Madrid and Valencia to "obtain their own benefit" and in which several workers of the Popular party would be implicated. Luis Bárcenas was accused of receiving EUR 1,300,000 from companies linked to Correa in exchange for receiving concessions from the party's public events.

Political Party: 
Partido Popular (PP).

Career:
Member of the General Courts, Senate of Spain for Cantabria (March 31, 2004 - April 19, 2010);
Treasurer of Partido Popular (PP) (June 2008 - July 28, 2009).


De acuerdo con elpais.com; Octubre 28, 2021: Luis Bárcenas fue sentenciado a dos años en prisión por falsedad documental, fraude y evasión de impuestos. La Audiencia Nacional dictó sentencia en relación a la reforma de la sede central del Partido Popular (PP) después de haber considerado probado que Bárcenas abono a la empresa Unifica más de un EUR 1,000,000 al margen de la facturación y contabilidad oficial, fondos que no fueron declarados a Hacienda Pública. Según la Audiencia, Bárcenas gestionó los fondos en efectivo que se aportaron al PP como donaciones privadas a través de una contabilidad paralela, de la cual, el ingreso y gasto no se dejó constancia en la contabilidad oficial y, por ende, no fueron fiscalizada por el Tribunal de Cuentas. Consecuentemente, se impuso para Bárcenas una multa de EUR 1,200,000 por haber sido cooperador necesario de un delito de falsedad contable en relación con otro contra Hacienda por el fraude al fisco del Impuesto de Sociedades de 2007 de Unifica.

De acuerdo con elconfidencial.com; Febrero 22, 2021: La Audiencia Nacional acordó poner en marcha la repatriación de EUR 50,342,107 que distintos condenados por el caso Gürtel, entre los que estaba Luis Bárcenas, tenían en Suiza. El objetivo era tener a disposición del tribunal las cantidades que habían permanecido bloqueadas en diversos bancos del mencionado país, en los que figuraban Credit Suisse, Lombard Odier, LGT Bank, Banque SYZ y Mirabaud. Según el decreto, alrededor de EUR 22,400,000 figuraban en cuentas de las que Bárcenas era titular.

De acuerdo con antena3.com; Febrero 08, 2021: En Febrero 08, 2021, Luis Bárcenas estaba enfrentando juicio por corrupción, falsedad documental y evasión fiscal. El caso estaba relacionado a la presunta caja B del Partido Popular (PP), motivo por el cual Bárcenas iba a tener que responder por el pago irregular de la reforma de la sede del PP en la calle Génova y por la compra de acciones de un medio con dinero de la caja B. Así mismo, Bárcenas exponía como responsables de una financiación irregular institucionalizada desde 1982, a la antigua cúpula encabezada por Mariano Rajoy.

De acuerdo con elmundo.es; Octubre 14, 2020: El Tribunal Supremo notificó la sentencia de la pieza Época I de la trama Gürtel (1999 – 2005), confirmando las condenas impuestas por la Audiencia Nacional a los principales líderes de la red de corrupción así como la del Partido Popular. La Sala mantuvo la condena del líder de la trama, sin embargo, redujo las condenas para varios de los implicados, entre ellos, Luis Bárcenas, a quien se redujo a 29 años y un mes en prisión. El Supremo tomó en consideración el recurso de Bárcenas, resultando en la reducción de la condena por blanqueo de capitales, exclusión del delito de falsedad documental y la absolución del delito de estafa procesal.

De acuerdo con nuevodiariodesalta.com.ar; Junio 02, 2018: Luis Bárcenas fue parte del caso donde la Empresa La Moraleja estuvo implicada en una trama de delitos de corrupción y lavado de dinero, en la cual Ángel Sanchis, Ángel Sanchis Herrero fueron los principales artífices tras desviar EUR 3,000,000 a través de la empresa mencionada. La sentencia menciona como pieza fundamental a Bárcenas, quien concedió la cantidad ya mencionada a Sanchis Perales en calidad de préstamo a nombre de la Fundación Sinequanon, sin embargo, los fondos salieron de la cuenta de Bárcenas a nombre de la fundación panameña que este último tenía en el Dresdner Bank de Suiza hacia otra del HSBC en Nueva York a cargo de Brixo SA, entidad en Uruguay vinculada a la familia Sanchís. Posteriormente, parte de los fondos fueron transferidos a cuentas de otra sociedad de los Sanchis, la argentina La Moraleja SA, a través de la cual, los individuos mencionados idearon una compleja trama para reintegrar el dinero a Bárcenas. Consecuentemente, todos los involucrados recibieron sus respectivas condenas después de comprobarse que estos conocían el origen ilícito de los fondos.

De acuerdo con vanitatis.elconfidencial.com; May 24, 2018: Luis Bárcenas fue sentenciado a 33 años en prisión por blanqueo de dinero, fraude fiscal, falsedad documental y estafa procesal. Luis Bárcenas y asociados estaban envueltos en la trama Gürtel y usaban al Grupo Correa y Partido Popular para emitir facturas infladas o que no respondían a servicios reales y se abonaban con cargo a los fondos públicos municipales.

De acuerdo con lainformacion.com; Octubre 02, 2016: El inicio del juicio del caso Gürtel fue programado en  Octubre 4, 2016. Los acusados fueron un total de 37 personas, incluyendo a José Luis Barcenas Gutierrez, todos acusados de fraude, corrupción, delitos financieros, soborno, falsificación y malversación de fondos por cometer actividades irregulares desarrolladas entre los años 1999 y 2005. La audiencia oral se llevaría a cabo en la sede en San Fernando de Henares.

De acuerdo con efe.com; Abril 27, 2015: La Fiscalía pidió cinco años de prisión y una multa de EUR 265,000 para José Luis Bárcenas Gutiérrez por el "caso Bárcenas". Basado en el fiscal, en el momento Bárcenas fue tesorero y gerente 1990-2009 del Partido Popular (PP), recibió fondos en efectivo por los empresarios que no podían hacer donaciones al partido ya que estaba en contra de la ley.
 
De acuerdo con lavozdegalicia.es; Marzo 06, 2015: El Juez de Audiencia Nacional ordenó el juicio de 40 personas por su presunta participación en un plan de sobornos en el seno del Partido Popular (PP). José Luis Bárcenas fue uno de los 40 individuos y jefe principal del caso.

De acuerdo con 20minutos.es; Enero 22, 2015: José Luis Bárcenas fue puesto en libertad bajo fianza por Pablo Ruz, juez de la Audiencia Nacional, después de pagar una fianza de EUR 200,000 impuesta por el Sr. Ruz. De acuerdo con elmundo.es; Febrero 26, 2014: Un informe de la Dirección Nacional de Investigación del Fraude (ONIF), reveló que el ex juez de la Audiencia Nacional ha rechazado por tercera vez una solicitud por Bárcenas Gutiérrez para ser puesto en libertad, después de la divulgación de dos cuentas bancarias en los Estados Unidos bajo su nombre. Tesorero del Partido Popular (PP) Bárcenas Gutiérrez defraudó a la Agencia Tributaria con un total de EUR 11,5 00,000 entre los años 2000 y 2011.

De acuerdo con lavozdegalicia.es; Diciembre 20, 2013: La Audiencia Nacional confirmó el confinamiento de José Luis Bárcenas Gutiérrez, ya que consideraban que pudiera escapar a un país que no permita su extradición.

De acuerdo con canarias24horas.com; Julio 30, 2013: El juez de la Audiencia Nacional, Pablo Ruz, decidió la exclusión de las cuentas bancarias en España y de los bienes de la ex tesorero del Partido Popular (PP), José Luis Bárcenas Gutiérrez, después de que el período de tiempo para pagar el unión civil de los EUR 43,200,000 impuesta por el Tribunal expiró.

De acuerdo con elpais.com; Julio 23, 2013: El juez encargado del caso Gürtel, Pablo Ruz, solicitó a las autoridades uruguayas congelar todas las cuentas bancarias bajo el nombre de José Luis Bárcenas Gutiérrez o su compañía Tesedul, que fue supuestamente el frente para el lavado de dinero.

De acuerdo con publico.pt; Junio 27, 2013: El ex tesorero del Partido Popular (PP), José Luis Bárcenas, fue arrestado por riesgo de fuga. Bárcenas fue acusado por el presunto envío de grandes sumas de dinero de las cuentas del partido político a Suiza y EE.UU. Fue enviado a prisión sin fianza, ya que había un riesgo grave de fuga o la posible manipulación y alteración de pruebas de una falsa compra y venta de obras de arte. Bárcenas fue a declarar el 27 de Junio, 2013, por la entrada de EUR 500,000 en su cuenta en las notas de EUR 500, durante el año 2006. Bárcenas reclamó el dinero de las ventas de obras de arte. De acuerdo con elpais.com; Junio 13, 2013: De acuerdo con el informe de la Agencia Tributaria española, José Luis Bárcenas y su esposa, Rosalía Iglesias, defraudaron al Servicio de Impuestos Internos española con EUR 1,500,000 en 2002 y 2003. details.enforcement: Disciplined/Financial Crimes | UK-Financial Conduct Authority | United Kingdom

hit.profile_notes: According to the United Kingdom-Financial Conduct Authority; September 27, 2024: The Authority hereby imposes on Starling Bank Limited (“Starling”) a financial penalty of GBP 28,959,426 pursuant to section 206 of the Act. Starling agreed to resolve this matter and qualified for a 30% (stage 1) discount under the Authority’s executive settlement procedures. Were it not for this discount, the Authority would have imposed a financial penalty of GBP 40,959,426 on Starling. Starling grew quickly, from approximately 43,000 customers in 2017 to 3.6 million in 2023. However, measures to tackle financial crime did not keep pace with its growth. When the FCA reviewed financial crime controls at challenger banks in 2021, it identified serious concerns with the anti-money laundering and sanctions framework in place at Starling. The bank agreed to a requirement restricting it from opening new accounts for high-risk customers until this improved. Starling failed to comply and opened over 54,000 accounts for 49,000 high-risk customers between September 2021 and November 2023. In January 2023, Starling became aware that its automated screening system had, since 2017, only been screening customers against a fraction of the full list of those subject to financial sanctions. A subsequent internal review identified systemic issues in its financial sanctions framework. Starling has since reported multiple potential breaches of financial sanctions to the relevant authorities.

details.enforcement: Environmental Crimes | US-U.S. Environmental Protection Agency | United States

hit.profile_notes:
According to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency; January 21, 2010: The United States today filed two major Clean Air Act settlements to reduce air emissions from container glass and Portland cement plants throughout the country, announced Cynthia Giles, assistant administrator for the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA) Office of Enforcement and Compliance Assurance and Ignacia S. Moreno, Assistant Attorney General for the Environment and Natural Resources Division. The settlements cover 15 U.S. plants owned by Saint-Gobain Containers, Inc., the nation’s second largest container glass manufacturer, and all 13 U.S. plants owned by the Lafarge Company and two subsidiaries, the nation’s second largest manufacturer of Portland cement. These settlements are the first system-wide settlements for these sectors under the Clean Air Act and require pollution control upgrades, acceptance of enforceable emission limits and payment of civil penalties.

Lafarge has also agreed to pay a civil penalty of USD 5,075,000 within 30 days of entry of the consent decree. USD 3,383,000 will be paid to the United States, and the remainder will be paid to the state and local agencies participating in the settlement.

hit.name: Abdul Rahman
hit.position_or_allegation: Charged with terrorism - December 2024.
hit.profile_notes: According to the tribune.com.pk; December 11, 2024: In December 2024, Abdul Rahman was charged with terrorism. An official report has detailed the progress made on the Bisham suicide attack investigation, revealing that several suspects have been arrested, and a charge sheet against 20 of them will be presented to an anti-terrorism court for trial. The incident occurred on March 26, 2024, when a suicide attack on a coaster vehicle resulted in the deaths of five Chinese nationals and the Pakistani driver. The attack took place on the Karakoram Highway in Bisham, where sources stated a terrorist named "Muqti" had been killed. A case against the suicide blast was filed at the Counter-Terrorism Department police station in Swat. The report mentions that the convoy consisted of 12 vehicles, with nine carrying Chinese engineers and workers, totaling 26 foreign nationals. A motor vehicle and the suicide bombers remain, along with a mobile phone number, were found at the crime scene. The phone number helped identify the facilitators in contact with the suicide bomber. Geofencing and geotagging were also conducted for further investigations. The documents reveal that one suspect, Adil, was arrested, leading to further arrests in various locations, including Swabi, Battagram, Mansehra, Charsadda, and Kuchlak, Balochistan. A total of 29 suspects has been named in the case. The interim charge sheet, which has been handed over to the prosecution, includes suspect Abdul Rahman. The search for other facilitators involved in the attack is ongoing.

hit.name: Abdul Rahman
hit.position_or_allegation: Arrested for fraud - December 2023.
hit.profile_notes: According to the odishabytes.com; December 23, 2023: In December 2023, Abdul Rahman was arrested along with other associates in connection with a credit card fraud amounting to INR 80,000,000. The complainant alleged that a credit card was issued in his name without his knowledge, and he was denied loan over poor CIBIL score because of the transactions made using it. The outstanding dues of the credit card was INR 140,000. During investigation identified Biju Tripathy as the person using the credit card. During the raid on his house, 450 credit and debit cards, INR 700,000 cash, 50 cheque books, 78 passbooks, 3 sacks of money receipt, six swipe machines and as many mobile phones were seized. Prasanjit Dash used to collect personal credentials of different persons to apply for credit cards and also fraudulently received those cards and used it. Simultaneously Pradeep Kumar Samantara, who was the employee of a bank, used to issue those cards in the name of Rakesh Kumar with forged documents. Mukesh Mantri introduced Prasanjit Dash with Biju Tripathy, who used to collect cash by using the credit card at POS counters like hospitals and OMFED booths in connivance with billing agents. Abdul Rahman and Rajesh Dash are hospital employees who worked as billing agents. Biju Tripathy used pay some commission to the billing agents and invest the remaining cash to earn profits. Police have calculated INR 20,000,000 of the money receipt seized.

According to the available information, promotional events have been held in Germany, at least in the past. Information and documentation recently submitted indicate that the operators contact potential interested parties via messaging services to invite them to participate in an online video conference. Furthermore, it is claimed that WeFi is seeking to obtain a banking license for Germany. BaFin reiterates that, to date, WeFi holds no authorization to offer banking business or financial services as well as crypto asset services within the country, nor has any application for a banking license been submitted so far.

The website www.starlingcredit.com has been added to this list.

According to Italian Commissione Nazionale per le Società e la Borsa; September 12, 2022: On September 12, 2022, the Italian Commissione Nazionale per le Società e la Borsa placed Starling Credit on a list of unauthorized entities following a warning issued by the Financial Conduct Authority of the United Kingdom.

Starling Credit does not have the authorization to provide investment or financial services in or from Luxembourg.

According to United Kingdom Financial Conduct Authority, the Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority, International Organization of Securities Commissions and the Netherlands Authority for the Financial Markets; August 16, 2022: On August 16, 2022, Starling Credit (Clone) is not an authorized finance company in the United Kingdomand is not permitted to provide financial services in the United Kingdom, this entity is using the name of an authorized firm to defraud consumers. Almost all firms and individuals carrying out financial services activities in the United Kingdom have to be authorised or registered by the FCA. This firm is not authorised or registered by the FCA, but has been targeting people in the United Kingdom, claiming to be an authorised firm. They may use the name of the genuine firm, the firm reference number (FRN) FCA have given the authorised firm or other details. Starling Credit (Clone) is not authorized by the FCA to provide financial services. This entity is fraudulently using the name of an authorized firm to appear authorized. hit.profile_notes:
On November 27, 2007, the United States Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control designated Mohammad Nadeem Ghani associated with Pakistani drug kingpin Shahbaz Khan. Ghani was sentenced to 10 years in prison for drug trafficking and an additional five years in prison for money laundering.

According to arabnews and khaleejtimes.com; November 05, 2007; In 2006, 19-member gang that was arrested in an operation known as Octopus. Mohammed Nadim Ghani was involved in money laundering and drug trading. Ghani was an expert in shipping and has a criminal record especially in smuggling, importing and exporting stolen and expired products. According to the information gang members are planning to smuggle a huge quantity of drugs 2,500kg of hashish in containers of 90,000 towels from Pakistan to Holland.

hit.name: Giampiero Fiorani

hit.profile_notes:
According to ilgiorno.it; September 23, 2015: In September 2015, Giampiero Fiorani was sent on trial by the Prosecutors of Lodi, for subtraction fraudulent payment of taxes. According to the authorities, he transferred the two houses that he owned to his relatives without paying taxes.

According to ilgiorno.it; November 09, 2012: In November 2012 Giampiero Fiorani, former Head of Banca Popolare di Lodi, was sentenced by the Court of Appeal of Nice, to one year of imprisonment and a fine of EUR 300.000 euros for money laundering. The facts dates back in 2003, when the former banker bought for 3 million euro a seaside villa in Roquebrune-Cap-Martin, one of the most exclusive French Riviera. The operation was carried out through the company Liberty, owned in equal parts by two acquaintances of Fiorani. In 2006, Fiorani acquired 45% of the company from one of the two owners and few months later, he sold it to a real estate agent in Monaco.

According to ilfattoquotidiano.it; May 28, 2012: On May 28, 2011 Giampiero Fiorani, was sentenced, to one year and eight months of imprisonment for inside trading and embezzlement in the process called “Antonveneta”. One year later, on May 28, 2012 the sentence was reduced on appeal to one year.

hit.profile_notes:
According to the US-Florida Attorney General; September 15, 2016: Attorney General announced an action taken against a Palm Beach jewelry store and the owner, Christopher Kaufmann, for deceptive jewelry consignment practices. Kaufmann operated under four business names that include Christopher Kaufmann; Christopher Kaufmann, Le Salon; CK Le Salon LLC; and Nikolas, LLC. Kaufmann’s operation is located in Palm Beach County’s prestigious Worth Avenue retail district.

According to the complaint, the stores led the consumers to believe that their high-end jewelry would sell for the amount listed in the consignment agreements. However, once consumers turned jewelry into the businesses, the stores purportedly failed to pay consumers the full amount agreed to in the consignment agreements. After repeated requests to either return jewelry or pay the amount agreed in the consignment agreement, the stores allegedly claimed that the jewelry had been lost, stolen or sold and offered to repay consumers pursuant to an installment payment plan. The complaint alleges that the stores typically paid one payment pursuant to an installment agreement and made no further payments to consumers.

hit.name: TD Bank USA, National Association
addresses: 2035 Limestone Road, Wilmington, Delaware, 19808, United States [Business]
hit.position_or_allegation: Imposed USD 1,300,000,000 in penalty for violations of the Bank Secrecy Act - October 10, 2024.

details.enforcement: Disciplined | US-U.S. Financial Crimes Enforcement Network | United States || Disciplined | US-U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency | United States

hit.profile_notes:
According to United States - Financial Crimes Enforcement Network; October 10, 2024: Published on that date, The U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) assessed a record USD 1,3000,000,000 penalty against TD Bank, N.A. and TD Bank USA, N.A. for violations of the Bank Secrecy Act (BSA), the primary U.S. anti-money laundering (AML) law that safeguards the financial system from illicit use. TD Bank is among the largest banks in the United States.

As part of the settlement, TD Bank admits that it willfully failed to implement and maintain an AML program that met the minimum requirements of the BSA and FinCEN’s implementing regulations. FinCEN’s investigation revealed that TD Bank knew that its AML program was neither appropriately designed nor adequately resourced to mitigate the actual illicit finance risks that it faced on multiple fronts. Among other failures, TD Bank’s processing of peer-to-peer transactions (e.g., Venmo and Zelle), including transactions indicative of human trafficking, was insufficient, and as a result, TD Bank failed to identify and timely report these transactions to FinCEN. TD Bank also allowed significant backlogs of potentially suspicious activity to persist, thereby depriving law enforcement of necessary information. TD Bank knew that it was the subject of significant funnel account activity involving high-risk countries yet failed to take timely action to address this substantial risk. TD Bank also failed to timely detect suspicious activity involving its own employees. For example, in 2021, a TD Bank employee facilitated the laundering of narcotics proceeds in exchange for bribes. This employee opened numerous accounts, including for shell companies, that then engaged in millions of dollars’ worth of funnel account activity in a high-risk jurisdiction where TD Bank maintained no operations. TD Bank knew that this type of activity was not subject to appropriate controls and failed to mitigate this glaring risk. TD Bank failed to properly limit or report suspicious transactions and cash activity that included substantial criminal activity.

According to United States - Office of the Comptroller of the Currency; October 10, 2024: On October 10, 2024 the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) announced a cease and desist order and a USD 450,000,000 civil money penalty against TD Bank, N.A. and TD Bank USA, N.A. (bank), for deficiencies in the bank’s Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) and anti-money laundering (AML) compliance program.

The OCC determined that the bank failed to develop and maintain a BSA/AML program reasonably designed to assure and monitor compliance with the BSA and its implementing regulations. Deficiencies in the bank’s BSA/AML program included those related to internal controls and risk management practices; risk assessments; customer due diligence; customer risk ratings; suspicious activity identification, evaluation, and reporting; governance; staffing; independent testing; and training, among others. The OCC found that the bank had significant, systemic breakdowns in its transaction monitoring program. The bank processed hundreds of millions of dollars of transactions with clear indicia of highly suspicious activity, creating a potential for significant money laundering, terrorist financing, or other illicit financial transactions. According to United States –Financial Industry Regulatory Authority; January 1997: On November 19, 1996, Peter Dennis Mathews, James Gus Oliver, Robert Alan Williky, Mark Joseph Vanyo, Lyle Emery Bettenhausen, Sr. and Gloria Ann Williams. Mathews, Oliver, Williky, Vanyo, and Bettenhausen submitted an Offer of Settlement pursuant to which Oliver was fined USD 25,000, suspended from association with any NASD member in any capacity for 90 days, and required to requalify by exam. Without admitting or denying the allegations, Mathews, Oliver, Williky, Vanyo, and Bettenhausen consented to the described sanctions and to the entry of findings that, in connection with a public offering, Mathews and Williky knowingly effected transactions that they knew or should have known, or were reckless in not knowing, were non-bona fide and designed to create the appearance of a successful completion of the offering. 

The findings also stated that Mathews and Williky knowingly or recklessly bid for and purchased, induced orders to bid for and purchase, and sold or resold, 20 percent of the offering while the distribution continued after its purported closing. Furthermore, the NASD determined that Mathews, Oliver, and Vanyo, by means of manipulative, deceptive, and other fraudulent devices and contrivances, effected a series of transactions that created actual and apparent trading in a stock, artificially supported the price, and were effected for the purpose of inducing the purchase or sale of the stock to others. The NASD found that Mathews, Oliver, and Bettenhausen made statements of material fact that they knew, had reason to know, or were reckless in not knowing, were false to induce retail customers to make investment decisions. The NASD also determined that Mathews executed transactions in the accounts of public customers that were not authorized and were made in order to support a stock price, further the aforementioned manipulative scheme, and avoid net capital deficiencies by lowering his member firm’s inventory. The findings stated that Mathews also allowed an individual, who was precluded from functioning as a registered representative, to direct trading, update quotations, direct unauthorized transactions in customer accounts, and participate in selling group and retail sales efforts at his member firm. The individual also failed to establish, maintain, and enforce supervisory procedures to assure compliance with applicable rules, misused customer funds, and engaged in private securities transactions.

details.enforcement: Environmental Crimes/Disciplined | US-U.S. Federal Trade Commission | United States

hit.profile_notes:
According to United Stated-Michigan Attorney General; September 28, 2000: On September 28, 2000, The Department of Environmental Quality, Michigan announced that the Lafarge Corporation has agreed to settle an air pollution enforcement action resulting from the operation of its Portland cement manufacturing plant in Alpena. As a result of the settlement, the company has agreed to reduce emissions of hydrogen chloride (HCl) from its Portland cement kilns and to control dust levels around the facility.

Lafarge will pay more than USD 1,500,000 to install the control measures required by the settlement and will pay the State of Michigan USD 723,000 in penalties and fines.

According to United Stated-Federal Trade Commission; October 16, 1998: On October 16, 1998, LaFarge, Corp. has agreed to restructure its agreement to purchase certain assets of Holnam, Inc., to settle Federal Trade Commission charges that the purchase agreement violated federal antitrust laws and could drive up prices for cement in the Pacific Northwest. LaFarge Corp. is based in Reston, Virginia. It is one of the largest suppliers of cement for residential, commercial, institutional and public works construction, with 14 plants in the United States and Canada and sales of USD 1600000 in 1996. Holnam, headquartered in Dundee, Michigan, is the number one supplier of cement in the United States. It operates 19 cement plants in North America and had sales of USD 983000000 in 1996.

According to United Stated-Federal Trade Commission; October 16, 1998: On October 16, 1998, The Federal Trade Commission issued Complaint against Lafarge, S.A  having reason to believe that the Lafarge, S.A controls, Lafarge Corporation (collectively "Respondents"), has entered into an agreement to acquire cement production assets of Holnam, Inc., that the agreement violates Section 5 of the Federal Trade Commission Act, as amended, 15 U.S.C.  45, and that the acquisition, if consummated, would result in a violation of Section 5 of the Federal Trade Commission Act, as amended, 15 U.S.C. 45, and Section 7 of the Clayton Act, as amended, 15 U.S.C.  18, and it appearing to the Commission that a proceeding in respect thereof would be in the public interest, hereby issues its complaint,

THE PROPOSED ACQUISITION: On February 4, 1998, Lafarge and Holnam signed a Letter of Intent setting out the principal elements of a proposed transaction, whereby Lafarge would acquire Holnam's Seattle, Washington cement plant and related assets.

details.enforcement: Disciplined/Debarred/Securities Fraud | US –Financial Industry Regulatory Authority | United States

hit.profile_notes:
According to United States-Financial Industry Regulatory Authority; December 1998:
Name: James G. Oliver
Address: Grapeville, Texas
Action: Individuals Whose Registrations Were Revoked for Failure to Pay Fines, Costs And/Or Provide Proof of Restitution in Connection with Violations
Action Date: October 27, 1998

According to United States –Financial Industry Regulatory Authority; January 1997: On November 19, 1996, Peter Dennis Mathews, James Gus Oliver, Robert Alan Williky, Mark Joseph Vanyo, Lyle Emery Bettenhausen, Sr. and Gloria Ann Williams. Mathews, Oliver, Williky, Vanyo, and Bettenhausen submitted an Offer of Settlement pursuant to which Oliver was fined USD 25,000, suspended from association with any NASD member in any capacity for 90 days, and required to requalify by exam. Without admitting or denying the allegations, Mathews, Oliver, Williky, Vanyo, and Bettenhausen consented to the described sanctions and to the entry of findings that, in connection with a public offering, Mathews and Williky knowingly effected transactions that they knew or should have known, or were reckless in not knowing, were non-bona fide and designed to create the appearance of a successful completion of the offering. 

The findings also stated that Mathews and Williky knowingly or recklessly bid for and purchased, induced orders to bid for and purchase, and sold or resold, 20 percent of the offering while the distribution continued after its purported closing. Furthermore, the NASD determined that Mathews, Oliver, and Vanyo, by means of manipulative, deceptive, and other fraudulent devices and contrivances, effected a series of transactions that created actual and apparent trading in a stock, artificially supported the price, and were effected for the purpose of inducing the purchase or sale of the stock to others. The NASD found that Mathews, Oliver, and Bettenhausen made statements of material fact that they knew, had reason to know, or were reckless in not knowing, were false to induce retail customers to make investment decisions. The NASD also determined that Mathews executed transactions in the accounts of public customers that were not authorized and were made in order to support a stock price, further the aforementioned manipulative scheme, and avoid net capital deficiencies by lowering his member firm’s inventory. The findings stated that Mathews also allowed an individual, who was precluded from functioning as a registered representative, to direct trading, update quotations, direct unauthorized transactions in customer accounts, and participate in selling group and retail sales efforts at his member firm. The individual also failed to establish, maintain, and enforce supervisory procedures to assure compliance with applicable rules, misused customer funds, and engaged in private securities transactions.

hit.name: Juan Reyes
hit.position_or_allegation: Convicted and disqualified from holding public office for embezzlement and aggravated conspiracy.

details.enforcement: Conspiracy/Disqualified/Organized Crime/Embezzlement | PE-Ministerio Público, Fiscalia de la Nación (Perú) | Peru

hit.profile_notes:
According to Ministerio Público, Fiscalía de la Nación del Perú; February 11, 2026: The Provincial Prosecutor's Office Specializing in Corruption Crimes by Officials in Lambayeque obtained an 18-year prison sentence for the former mayor of the Provincial Municipality of San Ignacio, Carlos Martínez, for the crime of embezzlement. He was also fined 620 days and disqualified from holding public office for 10 years. Along with him, other officials were also convicted of the same crime. Among them were the former manager of Territorial Planning and Urban Infrastructure, Álvaro Cabrera; the former head of Settlements, José Larraín; the former head of Logistics, Wilfredo Rivera; the former head of Treasury, Roel Aldana; and the former assistant to the Works Settlement office, William Díaz, who received sentences of up to 18 years in prison and were disqualified from holding public office. Likewise, José Larraín, Juan Reyes, and Luis Ancajima were convicted as accomplices to the crime of aggravated conspiracy, as they were members of the criminal organization "Los topos de San Ignacio". Manuel Ilatoma Gálvez was also convicted in this case, receiving a sentence of four years and 25 days in prison and a three-year disqualification from public office. José Zeña, Juan Ramos, Juan Nanfuñay, and Daniel Pisfil were also convicted. According to the report, they all embezzled PEN 762,000 in public funds by simulating contracts for alleged services involving the preparation of layout plans and topographic surveys.


De acuerdo con Ministerio Público, Fiscalía de la Nación del Perú; Febrero 11, 2026: La Fiscalía Provincial Especializada en Delitos de Corrupción de Funcionarios de Lambayeque logró una condena de 18 años de prisión para el exalcalde de la Municipalidad Provincial de San Ignacio, Carlos Martínez, por el delito de peculado doloso por apropiación. Asimismo, se le impuso una multa de 620 días multa y una inhabilitación para el ejercicio de la función pública por 10 años. Junto a él, también se obtuvo la sentencia de otros funcionarios por el mismo delito. Entre ellos el exgerente de Acondicionamiento Territorial e Infraestructura Urbana, Álvaro Cabrera; el exjefe de Liquidaciones, José Larraín; el exjefe de Logística, Wilfredo Rivera; el exjefe de Tesorería, Roel Aldana; y el exasistente de la oficina de Liquidación de Obras, William Díaz, quienes recibieron penas de hasta 18 años de prisión y fueron inhabilitados para ejercer la función pública. Asimismo, José Larraín, Juan Reyes y Luis Ancajima fueron sentenciados como cómplices del delito de asociación ilícita en su forma agravada, ya que fueron miembros de la organización criminal "Los topos de San Ignacio". Por este caso, también fue condenado Manuel Ilatoma Gálvez, quien recibió una sentencia de cuatro años y 25 días de prisión y una inhabilitación por tres años. También fueron condenados José Zeña, Juan Ramos, Juan Nanfuñay, Daniel Pisfil. De acuerdo con el informe, todos ellos se apropiaron de PEN 762 000 de fondos públicos, mediante la simulación de contratos por presuntos servicios de elaboración de planos de replanteo y levantamiento topográfico.
sources: PE-Ministerio Público, Fiscalia de la Nación (Perú)

hit.position_or_allegation: Fined with EUR 30 per day for two years for fraud and forgery - October 06, 2020.
hit.profile_notes:
According to lavozdegalicia.es; October 06, 2020: The National Court fined Pescanova with EUR 30 per day for two years for fraud and forgery. In addition, 11 individuals also involved in the case were sentenced for accounting fraud that was designed to obtain bank financing for Pescanova, as well as the manipulation of accounts in order to attract investors. Due to the acts carried out by those involved in the case, in 2013 there were losses of almost EUR 800,000,000 and EUR 3,600,000, which led to the bankruptcy of Pescanova.

According to elcorreogallego.es; June 04, 2020: The Civil Chamber of the Supreme Court rejected the appeal presented by Nueva Pescanova to the sentence passed in December 2016, in which the request that the old company faced the payment of different amounts was rejected, an agreement that had place in 2015 between the two companies. The ruling dismissed the claim of EUR 1,090,000 withheld by Pescanova plus interest accrued since 2015 as well as another EUR 800,000 for administrative expenses.

According to lavozdegalicia.es; January 28, 2020: Pescanova SA, the old company, was going to go to trial in the National Court along with all the former senior officials of the multinational. The 19 people and the 11 legal entities were accused of having altered the financial statements between 2009 and 2012, to hide the company's millionaire losses. Pescanova SA, stated that Nueva Pescanova, which arose after the bankruptcy, was going to be in charge of the economic consequences of the hypothetical condemnatory sentence. Additionally, the judge imposed a fine of EUR 262,000,000 and EUR 348,200,000 of bail for Pescanova SA.

According to europapress.es; November 28, 2015: The National Securities Market Commission (CNMV) imposed two fines on Pescanova for a total amount of EUR 450,000 and two others to the former executive president of the company Manuel Fernández de Sousa-Faro for EUR 225,000 for infractions of the Securities Market Law , according to the Official State Gazette (BOE), both the Galician company and its then president have been fined for carrying out market manipulation practices between January 29 and April 29, 2009.


De acuerdo con lavozdegalicia.es; Octubre 06, 2020: La Audiencia Nacional multó a Pescanova con EUR 30 por día durante dos años por fraude y falsedad de documentos. Además 11 individuos también involucrados en la causa fueron sentenciados por el fraude contable que fue diseñado para obtener financiación bancaria para Pescanova, así como la manipulación de cuentas para poder captar inversores. Debido a los actos realizados por involucrados en el caso, en 2013 se produjeron perdidas de casi EUR 800,000,000 y EUR 3,600,000, lo que llevó a la quiebra a Pescanova.

De acuerdo con elcorreogallego.es; Junio 04, 2020: La Sala de lo Civil del Tribunal Supremo rechazó el recurso presentado por Nueva Pescanova a la sentencia dictada en Diciembre 2016, en la que se desestimaba la petición de que la antigua sociedad afrontara el pago de distintas cantidades, acuerdo que tuvo lugar en 2015 entre las dos empresas. El fallo desestimó la reclamación de EUR 1,090,000 retenidos por Pescanova más los intereses devengados desde 2015 así como otros EUR 800,000 para gastos administrativos.

De acuerdo con lavozdegalicia.es; Enero 28, 2020: Pescanova SA, la vieja sociedad, iba a ir a juicio en la Audiencia Nacional junto con todos los antiguos altos cargos de la multinacional. Las 19 personas y las 11 jurídicas estaban acusadas de haber alterado los estados financieros entre los años 2009 y 2012 para ocultar las perdidas millonarias de la empresa. Pescanova SA, manifestó que Nueva Pescanova, que surgió tras el concurso de acreedores, se iba a encargar de las consecuencias económicas de la hipotética sentencia condenatoria. Adicionalmente, el juez impuso una multa de EUR 262,000,000 y EUR 348,200,000 de fianza para Pescanova SA.

De acuerdo con europapress.es; Noviembre 28, 2015: La Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores (CNMV) impusó dos puntas a Pescanova por un monto total de EUR 450.000 y otras dos al ex presidente ejecutivo de la empresa Manuel Fernández de Sousa-Faro por EUR 225.000 por infracciones a la Ley del Mercado de Valores, según a la Gaceta Oficial del Estado (BOE), tanto la empresa gallega como su entonces presidente han sido multados por llevar a cabo prácticas de manipulación del Mercado entre Enero 29 y Abril 29, 2009.

hit.profile_notes:
According to elpais.com; October 28, 2021: Luis Bárcenas was sentenced to two years in prison for forgery, fraud and tax evasion. The National Court issued a ruling in relation to the reform of the headquarters of the Popular Party (PP) after having considered proven that Bárcenas paid the Unifica company more than EUR 1,000,000 outside of the official billing and accounting, funds that were not declared to the Public Treasury. According to the Hearing, Bárcenas managed the cash funds that were contributed to the PP as private donations through a parallel accounting, of which the income and expenses were not recorded in the official accounting and, therefore, were not audited by the Court of Accounts. Consequently, a fine of EUR 1,200,000 was imposed on Bárcenas for having been a necessary cooperator of a crime of accounting falsification in relation to another against the Treasury for the fraud to the treasury of the Unifica Corporation Tax of 2007.

According to elconfidencial.com; February 22, 2021: The National High Court agreed to commence the repatriation of EUR 50,342,107 that different convicted persons in the Gürtel case, among whom was Luis Bárcenas, had in Switzerland. The objective was to have at the disposal of the court the amounts that had been blocked in various banks in the aforementioned country, which included Credit Suisse, Lombard Odier, LGT Bank, Banque SYZ and Mirabaud. According to the decree, around EUR 22,400,000 were in accounts owned by Bárcenas.

According to antena3.com; February 08, 2021: On February 08, 2021, Luis Bárcenas was facing trial for corruption, forgery and tax evasion. The case was related to the alleged box B of the Popular Party (PP), which is why Bárcenas was going to have to answer for the irregular payment of the reform of the headquarters of the PP on Genova street and for the purchase of shares of a half with money from box B. Likewise, Bárcenas exposed as responsible for an irregular financing institutionalized since 1982, the old leadership headed by Mariano Rajoy.

According to elmundo.es; October 14, 2020: The Supreme Court notified the sentence of the piece Epoca I of the Gürtel plot (1999 - 2005), confirming the sentences imposed by the National High Court on the main leaders of the corruption network as well as that of the Popular Party. The Chamber upheld the sentence of the leader of the plot; however, it reduced the sentences for several of those involved, among them, Luis Bárcenas, who was reduced to 29 years and one month in prison. The Supreme Court took into consideration the appeal of Bárcenas, resulting in the reduction of the sentence for money laundering, exclusion of the crime of forgery and the acquittal of the crime of procedural fraud.

According to nuevodiariodesalta.com.ar; June 02, 2018: Luis Barcenas was part of the case where the La Moraleja Company was involved in a plot of crimes of corruption and money laundering, in which Ángel Sanchis, Ángel Sanchis Herrero were the main architects after diverting EUR 3,000,000 through the company mentioned. The ruling mentions Bárcenas as a fundamental piece, who granted the aforementioned amount to Sanchis Perales as a loan on behalf of the Sinequanon Foundation, however, the funds came out of the Bárcenas account in the name of the Panamanian foundation that the latter had in the Dresdner Bank of Switzerland towards another of the HSBC in New York in charge of Brixo SA, an entity in Uruguay linked to the Sanchís family. Subsequently, part of the funds were transferred to accounts of another Sanchis company, Argentina's La Moraleja SA, through which the aforementioned individuals devised a complex scheme to reimburse the money to Bárcenas. Consequently, all those involved received their respective convictions after it was verified that these knew the illicit origin of the funds.

According to vanitatis.elconfidencial.com; May 24, 2018: Luis Bárcenas was sentenced to 33 years in prison for money laundering, tax evasion, forgery and fraud. Luis Bárcenas and other associates were involved in the Gürtel case and used Grupo Correa and Partido Popular to issue inflated invoices or invoices that did not respond to real services and were paid out of municipal public funds.

According to lainformacion.com; October 02, 2016: The trial of the case Gürtel was schedule on October 04, 2016. The defendants were 37 people including Jose Luis Barcenas Gutierrez, who were accused of fraud, corruption, financial crimes, bribery, forgery and embezzlement for committing irregular activities developed between the years 1999 and 2005. The oral hearing would take place in the headquarters in San Fernando de Henares.

According to efe.com; April 27, 2015: The Prosecutor's Office requested 5 years in prison and fined EUR 265,000 against José Luis Bárcenas Gutiérrez for the "Bárcenas case". Based on the prosecutor, during 1990 to 2009, when Bárcenas was Treasurer and Manager of Partido Popular (PP), he received cash funds by entrepreneurs who could not made donations to the party, since it was against the law.
 
According to lavozdegalicia.es; March 06, 2015: The Judge of the National Audience ordered the trial of 40 individuals for alleged involvement in a kickback scheme at the heart of Partido Popular (PP). Jose Luis Barcenas was one of the 40 individuals and master head of the case.

According to 20minutos.es; January 22, 2015: A Judge of the National Audience gave José Luis Bárcenas bail, after paying EUR 200,000. Additionally, Bárcenas must appear before the National Court every Monday, Wednesday and Friday, give his address and remain in Spain. 

According to elmundo.es; February 26, 2014: A report of the National Department of Fraud Investigation (ONIF), revealed that the Former Judge of the National Audience has rejected for the third time a request by Bárcenas Gutiérrez to be release from prison, after disclosure of  two bank accounts in the United States under his name.  Bárcenas Gutiérrez defrauded the Spanish Internal Revenue Office with a total EUR 11,5 00,000 between 2000 and 2011. 

According to lavozdegalicia.es; December 20, 2013: The National Audience confirmed the confinement of Jose Luis Bárcenas Gutiérrez, since they considered he could escape to a country that would not allowed his extradition.

According to canarias24horas.com; July 30, 2013: A Judge of the National Audience decided to foreclosure of the bank accounts in Spain and property of the former Treasurer of Partido Popular (PP), Jose Luis Bárcenas Gutiérrez, after the period of time to pay the civil bond of EUR 43,200,000 imposed by the Court expired. 

According to elpais.com; July 23, 2013: The judge in charge of the Gürtel case, Pablo Ruz, requested to the Uruguayan authorities to freeze all the bank accounts under the name of Jose Luis Bárcenas Gutiérrez or his company Tesedul, which was allegedly the front for laundering money. 

According to publico.pt; June 27, 2013: The Former Treasurer of Partido Popular (PP), José Luis Bárcenas, was arrested for flight risk. Bárcenas was accused of allegedly sending large sums of money from the political party's accounts to Switzerland and USA. He was sent to prison without bail, as there was a serious risk of flight, or possible manipulation and alteration of evidence of a false purchase and sale of works of art. Bárcenas was to testify on June 27, 2013, about the entry of EUR 500,000 on his account in the notes of EUR 500 during 2006. Bárcenas claimed the money was from sales of art works. He was being investigated for allegedly committing crimes against the government and against public finance, money laundering, attempted fraud and misrepresentation in commercial document.

According to elpais.com; June 13, 2013: According to the report of the Spanish Tax Office, José Luis Bárcenas and his wife, Rosalía Iglesias, defrauded the Spanish Internal Revenue Service with EUR 1,500,000 in 2002 and 2003. The couple also got tax returns of EUR 21,795 during those years. 

According to 20minutos.es; January 16, 2013: According to the reports that judge Pablo Ruz sent to the authorities, the former senator Jose Luis Bárcenas had EUR 22,000,000 in Swiss bank accounts, that were transferred to another account when he was charged with corruption for his involvement in the Gürtel case. 

According to rtve.es; February 09, 2009: Luis Bárcenas was provisionally indicted for corruption, bribery and tax evasion within Operation Gürtel. The Gürtel case investigated a presumed plot of corruption and influence peddling led by the businessman Francisco Correa, who drew funds from public entities in the autonomous communities of Madrid and Valencia to "obtain their own benefit" and in which several workers of the Popular party would be implicated. Luis Bárcenas was accused of receiving EUR 1,300,000 from companies linked to Correa in exchange for receiving concessions from the party's public events.

Political Party: 
Partido Popular (PP).

Career:
Member of the General Courts, Senate of Spain for Cantabria (March 31, 2004 - April 19, 2010);
Treasurer of Partido Popular (PP) (June 2008 - July 28, 2009).


De acuerdo con elpais.com; Octubre 28, 2021: Luis Bárcenas fue sentenciado a dos años en prisión por falsedad documental, fraude y evasión de impuestos. La Audiencia Nacional dictó sentencia en relación a la reforma de la sede central del Partido Popular (PP) después de haber considerado probado que Bárcenas abono a la empresa Unifica más de un EUR 1,000,000 al margen de la facturación y contabilidad oficial, fondos que no fueron declarados a Hacienda Pública. Según la Audiencia, Bárcenas gestionó los fondos en efectivo que se aportaron al PP como donaciones privadas a través de una contabilidad paralela, de la cual, el ingreso y gasto no se dejó constancia en la contabilidad oficial y, por ende, no fueron fiscalizada por el Tribunal de Cuentas. Consecuentemente, se impuso para Bárcenas una multa de EUR 1,200,000 por haber sido cooperador necesario de un delito de falsedad contable en relación con otro contra Hacienda por el fraude al fisco del Impuesto de Sociedades de 2007 de Unifica.

De acuerdo con elconfidencial.com; Febrero 22, 2021: La Audiencia Nacional acordó poner en marcha la repatriación de EUR 50,342,107 que distintos condenados por el caso Gürtel, entre los que estaba Luis Bárcenas, tenían en Suiza. El objetivo era tener a disposición del tribunal las cantidades que habían permanecido bloqueadas en diversos bancos del mencionado país, en los que figuraban Credit Suisse, Lombard Odier, LGT Bank, Banque SYZ y Mirabaud. Según el decreto, alrededor de EUR 22,400,000 figuraban en cuentas de las que Bárcenas era titular.

De acuerdo con antena3.com; Febrero 08, 2021: En Febrero 08, 2021, Luis Bárcenas estaba enfrentando juicio por corrupción, falsedad documental y evasión fiscal. El caso estaba relacionado a la presunta caja B del Partido Popular (PP), motivo por el cual Bárcenas iba a tener que responder por el pago irregular de la reforma de la sede del PP en la calle Génova y por la compra de acciones de un medio con dinero de la caja B. Así mismo, Bárcenas exponía como responsables de una financiación irregular institucionalizada desde 1982, a la antigua cúpula encabezada por Mariano Rajoy.

De acuerdo con elmundo.es; Octubre 14, 2020: El Tribunal Supremo notificó la sentencia de la pieza Época I de la trama Gürtel (1999 – 2005), confirmando las condenas impuestas por la Audiencia Nacional a los principales líderes de la red de corrupción así como la del Partido Popular. La Sala mantuvo la condena del líder de la trama, sin embargo, redujo las condenas para varios de los implicados, entre ellos, Luis Bárcenas, a quien se redujo a 29 años y un mes en prisión. El Supremo tomó en consideración el recurso de Bárcenas, resultando en la reducción de la condena por blanqueo de capitales, exclusión del delito de falsedad documental y la absolución del delito de estafa procesal.

De acuerdo con nuevodiariodesalta.com.ar; Junio 02, 2018: Luis Bárcenas fue parte del caso donde la Empresa La Moraleja estuvo implicada en una trama de delitos de corrupción y lavado de dinero, en la cual Ángel Sanchis, Ángel Sanchis Herrero fueron los principales artífices tras desviar EUR 3,000,000 a través de la empresa mencionada. La sentencia menciona como pieza fundamental a Bárcenas, quien concedió la cantidad ya mencionada a Sanchis Perales en calidad de préstamo a nombre de la Fundación Sinequanon, sin embargo, los fondos salieron de la cuenta de Bárcenas a nombre de la fundación panameña que este último tenía en el Dresdner Bank de Suiza hacia otra del HSBC en Nueva York a cargo de Brixo SA, entidad en Uruguay vinculada a la familia Sanchís. Posteriormente, parte de los fondos fueron transferidos a cuentas de otra sociedad de los Sanchis, la argentina La Moraleja SA, a través de la cual, los individuos mencionados idearon una compleja trama para reintegrar el dinero a Bárcenas. Consecuentemente, todos los involucrados recibieron sus respectivas condenas después de comprobarse que estos conocían el origen ilícito de los fondos.

De acuerdo con vanitatis.elconfidencial.com; May 24, 2018: Luis Bárcenas fue sentenciado a 33 años en prisión por blanqueo de dinero, fraude fiscal, falsedad documental y estafa procesal. Luis Bárcenas y asociados estaban envueltos en la trama Gürtel y usaban al Grupo Correa y Partido Popular para emitir facturas infladas o que no respondían a servicios reales y se abonaban con cargo a los fondos públicos municipales.

De acuerdo con lainformacion.com; Octubre 02, 2016: El inicio del juicio del caso Gürtel fue programado en  Octubre 4, 2016. Los acusados fueron un total de 37 personas, incluyendo a José Luis Barcenas Gutierrez, todos acusados de fraude, corrupción, delitos financieros, soborno, falsificación y malversación de fondos por cometer actividades irregulares desarrolladas entre los años 1999 y 2005. La audiencia oral se llevaría a cabo en la sede en San Fernando de Henares.

De acuerdo con efe.com; Abril 27, 2015: La Fiscalía pidió cinco años de prisión y una multa de EUR 265,000 para José Luis Bárcenas Gutiérrez por el "caso Bárcenas". Basado en el fiscal, en el momento Bárcenas fue tesorero y gerente 1990-2009 del Partido Popular (PP), recibió fondos en efectivo por los empresarios que no podían hacer donaciones al partido ya que estaba en contra de la ley.
 
De acuerdo con lavozdegalicia.es; Marzo 06, 2015: El Juez de Audiencia Nacional ordenó el juicio de 40 personas por su presunta participación en un plan de sobornos en el seno del Partido Popular (PP). José Luis Bárcenas fue uno de los 40 individuos y jefe principal del caso.

De acuerdo con 20minutos.es; Enero 22, 2015: José Luis Bárcenas fue puesto en libertad bajo fianza por Pablo Ruz, juez de la Audiencia Nacional, después de pagar una fianza de EUR 200,000 impuesta por el Sr. Ruz. Además del dinero, Luis Bárcenas está obligado a presentarse ante la Corte Nacional todos los lunes, miércoles y viernes, dar su dirección y permanecer en España.

De acuerdo con elmundo.es; Febrero 26, 2014: Un informe de la Dirección Nacional de Investigación del Fraude (ONIF), reveló que el ex juez de la Audiencia Nacional ha rechazado por tercera vez una solicitud por Bárcenas Gutiérrez para ser puesto en libertad, después de la divulgación de dos cuentas bancarias en los Estados Unidos bajo su nombre. Tesorero del Partido Popular (PP) Bárcenas Gutiérrez defraudó a la Agencia Tributaria con un total de EUR 11,5 00,000 entre los años 2000 y 2011.

De acuerdo con lavozdegalicia.es; Diciembre 20, 2013: La Audiencia Nacional confirmó el confinamiento de José Luis Bárcenas Gutiérrez, ya que consideraban que pudiera escapar a un país que no permita su extradición.

De acuerdo con canarias24horas.com; Julio 30, 2013: El juez de la Audiencia Nacional, Pablo Ruz, decidió la exclusión de las cuentas bancarias en España y de los bienes de la ex tesorero del Partido Popular (PP), José Luis Bárcenas Gutiérrez, después de que el período de tiempo para pagar el unión civil de los EUR 43,200,000 impuesta por el Tribunal expiró.

De acuerdo con elpais.com; Julio 23, 2013: El juez encargado del caso Gürtel, Pablo Ruz, solicitó a las autoridades uruguayas congelar todas las cuentas bancarias bajo el nombre de José Luis Bárcenas Gutiérrez o su compañía Tesedul, que fue supuestamente el frente para el lavado de dinero.

De acuerdo con publico.pt; Junio 27, 2013: El ex tesorero del Partido Popular (PP), José Luis Bárcenas, fue arrestado por riesgo de fuga. Bárcenas fue acusado por el presunto envío de grandes sumas de dinero de las cuentas del partido político a Suiza y EE.UU. Fue enviado a prisión sin fianza, ya que había un riesgo grave de fuga o la posible manipulación y alteración de pruebas de una falsa compra y venta de obras de arte. Bárcenas fue a declarar el 27 de Junio, 2013, por la entrada de EUR 500,000 en su cuenta en las notas de EUR 500, durante el año 2006. Bárcenas reclamó el dinero de las ventas de obras de arte. Él está siendo investigado por blanqueo de capitales, crímenes contra la hacienda pública, fraude y falsedad en documento mercantil.

De acuerdo con elpais.com; Junio 13, 2013: De acuerdo con el informe de la Agencia Tributaria española, José Luis Bárcenas y su esposa, Rosalía Iglesias, defraudaron al Servicio de Impuestos Internos española con EUR 1,500,000 en 2002 y 2003. La pareja también tiene declaraciones de impuestos de EUR 21,795 euros durante esos años.

De acuerdo con 20minutos.es; Enero 16, 2013: De acuerdo con los informes de que el juez Pablo Ruz envió a las autoridades, el ex senador José Luis Bárcenas tenía EUR 22,000,000 en cuentas de bancos suizos, que fueron transferidos a otra cuenta, cuando fue acusado de corrupción por su participación en el caso Gürtel.

De acuerdo con rtve.es; Febrero 09, 2009: Luis Bárcenas fue imputado provisionalmente por corrupción, cohecho y fraude fiscal dentro de la Operación Gürtel. El caso Gürtel investigaba una presunta trama de corrupción y tráfico de influencias dirigida por el empresario Francisco Correa que se nutría de fondos de entidades públicas de las comunidades autónomas de Madrid y Valencia para "obtener un beneficio propio" y en la que estarían implicados varios cargos del Partido Popular. Luis Bárcenas estaba acusado de recibir EUR 1,300,000 de las empresas vinculadas con Correa a cambio de recibir concesiones de actos públicos del partido.

Partido Político: 
Partido Popular (PP).

Trayectoria:

Tesorero del Partido Popular (PP) (Junio 2008 - Julio 28, 2009).

details.enforcement: Bank Fraud/Disciplined | US-U.S. FDIC Temporary Order to Cease and Desist | United States || Disciplined/Bank Fraud | US-U.S. FDIC Order to Cease and Desist | United States || Bank Fraud/Disciplined | US-U.S. Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation | United States || Disciplined/Bank Fraud | US-Washington State Department of Financial Institutions Securities Division | United States

hit.profile_notes:
According to U.S. Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation; May 10, 2021: The Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation announced a settlement with Umpqua Bank for engaging in unfair and deceptive practices, in violation of Section 5 of the Federal Trade Commission Act (Section 5). Umpqua Bank stipulated to the issuance of an Order to Pay Civil Money Penalty (CMP) in the amount of USD 1,800,000.

The FDIC determined that Umpqua Bank engaged in Section 5 violations related to collection practices involving commercial equipment financing through its wholly owned subsidiary, Financial Pacific Leasing, Inc.. The FDIC determined that FinPac’s collection fee practices were unfair and deceptive. Specifically, FinPac charged various undisclosed collection fees to borrowers whose accounts were past due, such as collection call and letter fees and third-party collection fees.

The FDIC also determined that certain collection practices at FinPac were unfair and deceptive. FinPac engaged in excessive and sequential collection calls to customers, even when customers requested that FinPac stop these calls. FinPac also disclosed information about the customers’ debts to third parties. Lastly, FinPac advised borrowers FinPac would report delinquencies on commercial debt to the consumer reporting agencies, when its policy and practice was not to report such delinquencies to the consumer reporting agencies. Umpqua Bank agreed to the issuance of the Order without admitting or denying these violations. In addition, the Bank voluntarily paid restitution totaling approximately USD 1,628,000 to the 16,902 customers who were charged the undisclosed collection fees.

According to U.S. Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation; May 06, 2021; Umpqua Bank ordered to pay penalty of USD 1,800,000 for engaged in violations of Section 5 of the Federal Trade Commission Act. 

According to U.S. FDIC Temporary Order to Cease and Desist and U.S. Washington State Department of Financial Institutions Securities Division; September 27, 2010: The Cease and Desist order against Sterling Savings Bank has been terminated.

According to the U.S. FDIC Order to Cease and Desist and U.S. Washington State Department of Financial Institutions Securities Division; October 9, 2009: Cease and desist order issued against Sterling Savings Bank from the following unsafe and unsound banking practices, as more fully set forth in the joint FDIC and WDFI Report of Visitation dated June 29, 2009. The FDIC and the WDFI considered the matter and determined that they had reason to believe that the Bank had engaged in unsafe or unsound banking practices and violations of law and/or regulations. Sterling Savings Bank  failed to maintain the minimum capital ratio, failed to submit an acceptable capital plan and failed to implement or adhere to a capital plan to which the Regional Director and the Director of Banks have taken no written objection.

The defendants were sentenced to three year term of probation and to pay financial penalties, including criminal fines of USD 90 780 000 and forfeiture of USD 687 000 000 totaling USD 777 780 000. The defendants’ scheme to pay ISIS and ANF in exchange for permission to operate a cement plant in Syria from August 2013 to October 2014, which enabled LCS to obtain approximately USD 70 300 000 in revenue. 

As a result of the scheme, LCS obtained approximately USD 70 300 000 in total sales revenue from August 2013 through 2014.  The gains to all participants in the conspiracy, including LCS, the intermediaries and the terrorist groups, totaled approximately USD 80 540 000.

hit.profile_notes:
According to U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission; December 21, 2021: The Securities and Exchange Commission announced that Nikola Corporation has agreed to pay USD 125,000,000 to settle charges that it defrauded investors by misleading them about its products, technical advancements, and commercial prospects. 

According to the SEC’s order, before Nikola had produced a single commercial product Trevor Milton, the company’s founder and former Chief Executive Officer and Executive Chairman embarked on a public relations campaign aimed at inflating and maintaining Nikola’s stock price. The order finds that Milton misled investors about Nikola’s technological advancements, in-house production capabilities, hydrogen production, truck reservations and orders, and financial outlook. The order also finds that Nikola further misled investors by misrepresenting or omitting material facts about the refueling time of its prototype vehicles, the status of its headquarters’ hydrogen station, the anticipated cost and sources of electricity for its planned hydrogen production, and the economic risks and benefits associated with its contemplated partnership with a leading auto manufacturer.

Accordingly it is hereby ordered that Nikola cease and desist from committing or causing any violations and any future violations of Section of the Exchange Act and shall pay a civil money penalty in the amount of USD 125,000,000 to the Securities and Exchange Commission.

According to cnbc.com and dailymail.co.uk; September 15, 2020: Nikola Corporation is under investigation by U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) into short seller claims that the company misled investors. The SEC was looking into whether Nikola may have violated securities laws. Federal investigators are examining whether Nikola, which manufactures electric and hydrogen-powered semi-trucks, misrepresented facts about progress it had made in developing the much-touted technology.

hit.profile_notes:
On July 25, 2018, the United States Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control imposed sanctions against Anni Beurklian. Anni Beurklian was a key component of a vast network procuring electronics on behalf of Syria’s Scientific Studies and Research Center (SSRC), the agency responsible for the development of Syria’s chemical weapons.

According to United States United States Attorney - District of Massachusetts; June 11, 2020: On June 11, 2020, filed a civil forfeiture action against Anni Beurklian and her husband Antoine Ajaka in connection with a scheme to smuggle goods out of the United States and to supply services to Syria. The United States also seized the U.S. website of the Syrian-based company Electronic Katranji Trading (“EKT”), ekt2.com, on probable cause that it was used to facilitate the illegal export of merchandise from the United States.The couple operated Top Tech US Inc. (“Top Tech”), a U.S. company, from the Waltham home. Beurklian, Ajaka and Top Tech were indicted in March 2018 on conspiracy to violate U.S. export laws and regulations, conspiracy to defraud the United States, smuggling U.S. goods out of the United States, illegally providing services to persons located in Syria, mail fraud, conspiracy to obstruct justice and obstruction of justice.

The civil forfeiture action and website seizure are pursuant to Title 19 of the United States Code, which provides that property used to facilitate the exporting or sending of merchandise from the United States contrary to law shall be seized and forfeited to the United States.

According to United States Department of State Directorate of Defense Trade Controls; November, 2019: On March 21, 2018 Anni Beurkl and her husband, Antoine Ajaka their company Top Tech US Inc, and a Syrian national Amir Katranji were indicted on conspiracy to violate U.S. export laws and regulations, conspiracy to defraud the United States, smuggling U.S. goods out of the United States, conspiracy to obstruct justice, and obstruction of justice. Beurklian, Ajaka, and Top Tech US Inc. also are charged with illegally providing services to persons located in Syria and mail fraud.

According to United States Attorney - District of Massachusetts; March 21, 2018: Anni Beurklian and her husband, Antoine Ajaka, their company Top Tech US Inc, and a Syrian national Amir Katranji were indicted on conspiracy to violate U.S. export laws and regulations, conspiracy to defraud the United States, smuggling U.S. goods out of the United States, conspiracy to obstruct justice, and obstruction of justice. Beurklian, Ajaka, and Top Tech US Inc. are also charged with illegally providing services to persons located in Syria and mail fraud. Beurklian and Ajaka previously fled the U.S. and have not returned. 

As alleged in the indictment, beginning no later than 2012 and continuing until Jan. 09, 2018, Beurklian and her husband operated an export business, Top Tech US Inc., out of their Waltham residence. The couple used their business to procure goods, including electronics, computer equipment, and electrical switches, from U.S. companies and export those goods out of the United States to customers in Lebanon and Syria. 

The indictment further alleges that in or about 2013, Ajaka and Beurklian began doing business with Katranji and supplying U.S. origin goods to EKT using Top Tech US. Ajaka and Beurklian knew that Katranji operated a business in Syria and that they were providing brokering services to Katranji and his Syrian company, EKT, by buying and shipping U.S. origin goods to EKT and its customers. EKT paid Ajaka and Beurklian more than USD 200,000 through Top Tech US bank accounts for their services. To conceal their illegal activity with EKT and evade the mandatory export filing requirement, Ajaka and Beurklian, with the knowledge and agreement of Katranji, falsified shipping paperwork and undervalued goods being shipped overseas directly to, or on behalf of, EKT.
